translations.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 210
translations.idiomatic: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 210

sentences.zh: 卷第二百一十

translations.literal: Volume 210
translations.idiomatic: Volume Two Hundred Ten

sentences.zh: 【唐紀二十六】 起上章閹茂八月，盡昭陽赤奮若，凡三年有奇。

translations.literal: [Tang Records 26] Beginning in the eighth month of the year Shangzhang Yanmao, ending in Zhaoyang Chifenruo, altogether a little more than three years.
translations.idiomatic: [Tang Records 26] From the eighth month of 710 through 713—a span of a little more than three years.

sentences.zh: 八月，庚寅，往巽第按問。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on the day gengyin, [officials] went to Pei Xun's residence to conduct inquiries.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on the gengyin day, investigators went to Pei Xun's mansion to question those involved in the plot.

sentences.zh: 重福奄至，縣官馳出，白留守；

translations.literal: Chongfu arrived suddenly; county officials galloped out and reported to the acting governor.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Chongfu appeared without warning; local officers raced out to alert the Eastern Capital's acting governor.

sentences.zh: 群官皆逃匿，洛州長史崔日知獨帥眾討之。

translations.literal: The officials all fled and hid; only Cui Rizhi, the Luozhou chief secretary, alone led the troops to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Most officials scattered in panic, but Cui Rizhi, chief secretary of Luozhou, alone rallied a force to oppose him.

sentences.zh: 留台侍御史李邕遇重福於天津橋，從者已數百人，馳至屯營，告之曰：「譙王得罪先帝，今無故入都，此必為亂；

translations.literal: The acting censor Li Yong met Chongfu at Tianjin Bridge; his followers already numbered several hundred. He galloped to the garrison camp and told them, "The Prince of Qiao offended the late emperor; now he has entered the capital without cause—this must be rebellion;
translations.idiomatic: Li Yong, the censor left in charge at the eastern capital, met Chongfu on Tianjin Bridge with several hundred men already at his back. He raced to the garrison camps and urged the soldiers: "The Prince of Qiao was condemned by the late emperor; his sudden entry into the capital can only mean revolt—

sentences.zh: 君等宜立功取富貴。」

translations.literal: you gentlemen ought to win merit and gain wealth and rank."
translations.idiomatic: you should win your reward and rise in rank now."

sentences.zh: 又告皇城使閉諸門。

translations.literal: He also told the commissioner of the Imperial City to shut all the gates.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered the Imperial City commissioner to seal every gate.

sentences.zh: 重福先趣左、右屯營，營中射之，矢如雨下。

translations.literal: Chongfu first hastened to the left and right garrison camps; the camps shot at him, arrows falling like rain.
translations.idiomatic: Chongfu rushed first to the left and right garrison camps, but the troops inside rained arrows down on him.

sentences.zh: 乃還趣左掖門，欲取留守兵，見門閉，大怒，命焚之。

translations.literal: He then turned back and hastened to the Left Flank Gate, intending to seize the acting governor's troops; seeing the gate closed, he flew into a rage and ordered it burned.
translations.idiomatic: He turned back toward the Left Flank Gate to seize the governor's troops; finding the gate shut, he raged and ordered it set ablaze.

sentences.zh: 火未及然，左屯營兵出逼之，重福窘迫，策馬出上東，逃匿山谷。

translations.literal: Before the fire could catch, soldiers from the left garrison camp came out and pressed him; Chongfu, hard pressed, spurred his horse out through Shangdong and fled into the hills.
translations.idiomatic: Before the flames could spread, the left garrison sallied against him; cornered, Chongfu spurred his horse out the upper east gate and vanished into the hills.

sentences.zh: 明日，留守大出兵搜捕，重福赴漕渠溺死。

translations.literal: The next day the acting governor sent out large forces to hunt him down; Chongfu threw himself into the canal and drowned.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the acting governor launched a full search; Chongfu drowned himself in the transport canal.

sentences.zh: 日知，日用之從父兄也，以功拜東都留守。

translations.literal: Rizhi was a paternal cousin of Li Riyong; for his merit he was appointed acting governor of the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Rizhi was a cousin of Li Riyong on the father's side and was made acting governor of Luoyang for his service.

sentences.zh: 鄭愔貌醜多須，既敗，梳髻，著婦人服，匿車中；

translations.literal: Zheng Yin was ugly in appearance and heavily bearded; once defeated, he dressed his hair in a woman's coiffure, put on women's clothes, and hid in a carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Yin was homely and heavily bearded; when the plot collapsed he bound his hair like a woman, dressed in female robes, and hid in a cart.

sentences.zh: 擒獲，被鞫，股慄不能對。

translations.literal: He was seized, interrogated, and his legs trembled so that he could not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Captured and put to the question, his legs shook so violently he could not speak.

sentences.zh: 張靈均神氣自若，顧愔曰：「吾與此人舉事，宜其敗也！」

translations.literal: Zhang Lingjun remained calm in bearing and, turning to Yin, said, "To raise a revolt with this man—no wonder we were defeated!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Lingjun kept his composure and, glancing at Yin, said, "Plotting with this fellow—of course we failed!"

sentences.zh: 與愔皆斬於東都市。

translations.literal: He and Yin were both beheaded in the eastern capital marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: Both men were beheaded in Luoyang's eastern market.

sentences.zh: 初，愔附來俊臣得進；

translations.literal: Earlier, Yin had attached himself to Lai Junchen to advance.
translations.idiomatic: Yin had first risen by clinging to Lai Junchen.

sentences.zh: 俊臣誅，附張易之；

translations.literal: When Junchen was executed, he attached himself to Zhang Yizhi.
translations.idiomatic: When Junchen fell, he shifted to Zhang Yizhi.

sentences.zh: 易之誅，附韋氏；

translations.literal: When Yizhi was executed, he attached himself to the Wei clan.
translations.idiomatic: When Yizhi was killed, he backed Empress Wei's faction.

sentences.zh: 韋氏敗，又附譙王重福，竟坐族誅。

translations.literal: When the Wei clan fell, he again attached himself to Prince Chongfu of Qiao and in the end was punished with extermination of his clan.
translations.idiomatic: After the Wei clan's ruin he cast his lot with Prince Chongfu—and at last brought extinction on his entire house.

sentences.zh: 嚴善思免死，流靜州。

translations.literal: Yan Shansi was spared death and banished to Jing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Shansi was spared execution and exiled to Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 萬騎恃討諸韋之功，多暴橫，長安中苦之；

translations.literal: The Ten Thousand Riders relied on their merit in suppressing the Wei faction and were mostly violent and overbearing; the people of Chang'an suffered under them.
translations.idiomatic: The Ten Thousand Riders, proud of their part in crushing the Wei faction, bullied the capital until the city groaned under them.

sentences.zh: 詔並除外官。

translations.literal: An edict stripped them all of their extra official posts.
translations.idiomatic: An edict stripped them of every supplemental office they held.

sentences.zh: 又停以戶奴為萬騎；

translations.literal: Recruitment of household slaves as Ten Thousand Riders was also halted.
translations.idiomatic: The practice of drafting household slaves into the Ten Thousand Riders was abolished.

sentences.zh: 更置飛騎，隸左、右羽林。

translations.literal: Flying Cavalry was re-established instead and placed under the left and right Imperial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: The Flying Cavalry was reinstated and placed under the left and right Imperial Guard.

sentences.zh: 姚元之、宋璟及御史大夫畢構上言：「先朝斜封官悉宜停廢。」

translations.literal: Yao Chongzhi, Song Jing, and the censor-in-chief Bi Gou submitted a memorial: "All irregularly appointed officials of the previous reign ought to be abolished."
translations.idiomatic: Yao Yuanzhi, Song Jing, and Censor-in-Chief Bi Gou urged: "Every 'slant-seal' appointee from the late reign should be dismissed."

sentences.zh: 上從之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，罷斜封官凡數千人。

translations.literal: On the day guisi, several thousand irregular appointees were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi day, several thousand such appointees were removed from office.

sentences.zh: 刑部尚書、同中書門下三品裴談貶蒲州刺史。

translations.literal: Pei Tan, minister of justice and fellow chief minister of the Secretariat-Chancellery, was demoted to prefect of Pu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Tan, Minister of Justice and chief minister, was demoted to prefect of Pu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 贈蘇安恆諫議大夫。

translations.literal: Su Anheng was posthumously granted the title of remonstrance official.
translations.idiomatic: Su Anheng was posthumously made Remonstrance Official.

sentences.zh: 九月，辛未，以太子少師致仕唐休璟為朔方道大總管。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on the day xinwei, the retired grand mentor of the heir apparent Tang Xiujing was made grand general of the Shuofang circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on xinwei day, the retired Grand Mentor Tang Xiujing was appointed grand general of the Shuofang frontier command.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，甲申，禮儀使姚元之、宋璟奏：「大行皇帝神主，應祔太廟，請遷義宗神主於東都，別立廟。」

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on the day jiashen, the ritual commissioners Yao Chongzhi and Song Jing memorialized: "The spirit tablet of the late emperor should be enshrined in the Grand Ancestral Temple; we request that the tablet of Emperor Yizong be moved to the Eastern Capital and given a separate temple."
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter, on jiashen day, ritual commissioners Yao Yuanzhi and Song Jing argued: "The late emperor's tablet belongs in the Grand Ancestral Temple. We ask that Emperor Yizong's tablet be moved to Luoyang with a temple of its own."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved.

sentences.zh: 乙未，追復天後尊號為大聖天後。

translations.literal: On the day yiwei, the honorific title of the late Empress was restored as Great Sage Heavenly Empress.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei day, Empress Wu's title was restored as Great Sage Heavenly Empress.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，以幽州鎮守經略節度大使薛訥為左武衛大將軍兼幽州都督。

translations.literal: On the day dingyou, Xue Ne, frontier commissioner for defense and pacification of Youzhou, was made general of the Left Martial Guard and concurrently regional commander of Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou day, Xue Ne, Youzhou frontier commissioner, was made general of the Left Martial Guard and concurrent protector of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 節度使之名自訥始。

translations.literal: The title of frontier commissioner (jiedushi) began with Ne.
translations.idiomatic: The title jiedushi—military governor—dates from Xue Ne's appointment.

sentences.zh: 太平公主以太子年少，意頗易之；

translations.literal: Princess Taiping, because the crown prince was young, thought him quite easy to manage.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Taiping assumed the young crown prince would be easy to control.

sentences.zh: 既而憚其英武，欲更擇闇弱者立之以久其權，數為流言，云「太子非長，不當立。」

translations.literal: Later she came to fear his martial spirit and wished to choose a weaker, duller man to install so as to prolong her power; she spread rumors many times, saying, "The crown prince is not the eldest son and ought not to be established."
translations.idiomatic: She soon feared his force of character and hoped to set up a weaker prince to keep her grip on power, spreading rumors that "the heir is not the eldest son and should not succeed."

sentences.zh: 己亥，制戒諭中外，以息浮議。

translations.literal: On the day jihai an edict admonished the court and the realm to quiet idle talk.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai day an edict warned the court and the realm to cease such gossip.

sentences.zh: 公主每覘伺太子所為，纖介必聞於上，太子左右，亦往往為公主耳目，太子深不自安。

translations.literal: The princess constantly watched the crown prince's conduct; the slightest detail was sure to reach the emperor. Many of those around the crown prince were also the princess's eyes and ears, and the crown prince was deeply ill at ease.
translations.idiomatic: She spied on his every move and reported the least detail to the throne; many in his own household served as her informants, and the heir lived in constant unease.

sentences.zh: 謚故太子重俊曰節愍。

translations.literal: The late crown prince Chongjun was given the posthumous name Jiemin.
translations.idiomatic: The late Crown Prince Chongjun was posthumously titled Jiemin (Steadfast and Lamented).

sentences.zh: 太府少卿萬年韋湊上書，以為：「賞罰所不加者，則考行立謚以褒貶之。

translations.literal: Wei Cou of Wannian, vice minister of the Court of the Imperial Treasury, submitted a memorial, arguing: "Where reward and punishment do not reach, conduct is examined and a posthumous name is conferred to praise or condemn.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Cou, Vice Minister of the Imperial Treasury, argued in a memorial: "When the living law cannot reach a man, posterity judges him by his posthumous name.

sentences.zh: 故太子重俊，與李多祚等稱兵入宮，中宗登玄武門以避之，太子據鞍督兵自若；

translations.literal: The former crown prince Chongjun, with Li Duozhuo and others, raised troops and entered the palace; Emperor Zhongzong ascended the Xuanwu Gate to avoid them, while the crown prince sat his saddle and directed the army as if at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Former Crown Prince Chongjun marched into the palace with Li Duozhuo and others; Emperor Zhongzong fled to the Xuanwu Gate while Chongjun sat his saddle and directed the assault without flinching.

sentences.zh: 及其徒倒戈，多祚等死，太子方逃竄。

translations.literal: When his followers turned their weapons, Duozhuo and the others were killed, and only then did the crown prince flee.
translations.idiomatic: Only when his men turned on him and Duozhuo fell did the prince finally run.

sentences.zh: 向使宿衛不守，其為禍也胡可忍言！

translations.literal: Had the palace guard not held firm, what disaster could be endured in the telling!
translations.idiomatic: Had the palace guard failed, the catastrophe is beyond words.

sentences.zh: 明日，中宗雨泣，謂供奉官曰：『幾不與卿等相見。』

translations.literal: The next day Emperor Zhongzong wept in the rain and said to his attendants, "I nearly never saw you again."
translations.idiomatic: The next day Zhongzong wept openly and told his attendants, "I nearly never saw you again."

sentences.zh: 其危如此，今聖朝禮葬，謚為節愍，臣竊惑之。

translations.literal: The danger was so great; now the holy court gives him a state funeral and the posthumous name Jiemin—I am privately perplexed.
translations.idiomatic: The peril was that grave—yet the court now buries him with full honors as Jiemin. I cannot make sense of it.

sentences.zh: 夫臣子之禮，過廟必下，過位必趨。

translations.literal: The ritual of subject and minister requires dismounting when passing a temple and quickening pace when passing the ruler's place.
translations.idiomatic: A loyal subject dismounts when passing the ancestral temple and quickens his step before the throne.

sentences.zh: 漢成帝之為太子，不敢絕馳道。

translations.literal: When Emperor Cheng of Han was crown prince, he did not dare block the imperial carriage road.
translations.idiomatic: Even as crown prince, Emperor Cheng of Han would not block the imperial carriage road.

sentences.zh: 而重俊稱兵宮內，跨馬御前，無禮甚矣。

translations.literal: Yet Chongjun raised troops within the palace and rode a horse before the emperor—his lack of ritual was extreme.
translations.idiomatic: Chongjun raised arms inside the palace and rode before his father—an outrage against all propriety.

sentences.zh: 若以其誅武三思父子而嘉之，則興兵以誅奸臣而尊君父可也；

translations.literal: If one praises him for killing Wu Sansi and his son, then raising troops to execute treacherous ministers and honor one's sovereign father would be permissible.
translations.idiomatic: If we honor him for killing the Wu Sansis, then any prince who takes up arms to purge traitors might claim the same merit.

sentences.zh: 今欲自取之，是與三思競為逆也，又足嘉乎！

translations.literal: Now he wished to seize the throne for himself—he was competing with Sansi in rebellion; how can that be praised!
translations.idiomatic: But he sought the throne for himself—he was no better than Sansi. What is there to praise?

sentences.zh: 若以其欲廢韋氏而嘉之，則韋氏於時逆狀未彰，大義未絕，苟無中宗之命而廢之，是脅父廢母也，庸可乎！

translations.literal: If one praises him for wishing to depose the Wei clan, at that time the Wei's treason was not yet manifest and the great bond was not yet severed; to depose them without Zhongzong's command would be coercing one's father and deposing one's mother—how could that be allowed!
translations.idiomatic: If we praise his plan to depose Empress Wei, remember that her guilt was not yet proven and the bond of filial piety still held—deposing her without the emperor's order would have been forcing a father and casting out a mother. How can that be right?

sentences.zh: 漢戾太子困於江充之讒，發忿殺充，雖興兵交戰，非圍逼君父也；

translations.literal: The Han crown prince Li, trapped by Jiang Chong's slander, in anger killed Chong; though he raised troops and fought, he did not besiege and press his sovereign father.
translations.idiomatic: Han's Crown Prince Li, driven by Jiang Chong's slanders, killed Chong in rage; though he took up arms, he never pressed his father.

sentences.zh: 兵敗而死，及其孫為天子，始得改葬，猶謚曰戾。

translations.literal: Defeated in battle he died; only when his grandson became emperor was he reburied, and still he was given the posthumous name Li (Rebellious).
translations.idiomatic: He died in defeat; only when his grandson became emperor was he reburied—and still he was called Li, "the Rebellious."

sentences.zh: 況重俊可謚之曰節愍乎！

translations.literal: How much less can Chongjun be given the posthumous name Jiemin!
translations.idiomatic: How then can Chongjun deserve the name Jiemin?

sentences.zh: 臣恐後之亂臣賊子，得引以為比，開悖逆之原，非所以彰善癉惡也，請改其謚。

translations.literal: I fear that later rebellious ministers and traitorous sons will cite him as a precedent and open the source of defiance—this is not how to display good and repel evil. I request that his posthumous name be changed.
translations.idiomatic: Future rebels will cite this precedent and the floodgates of treason will open. I beg that his posthumous name be changed.

sentences.zh: 多祚等從重俊興兵，不為無罪。

translations.literal: Duozhuo and the others who followed Chongjun in raising troops were not without guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Duozhuo and those who followed Chongjun were hardly innocent.

sentences.zh: 陛下今宥之可也，名之為雪，亦所未安。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty may pardon them now, but to give them the posthumous name Xue (Vindicated) is also unsettling."
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty may forgive them, but to call them "Vindicated" in death is still wrong."

sentences.zh: 上甚然其言，而執政以為制命已行，不為追改，但停多祚等贈官而已。

translations.literal: The emperor greatly approved his words, but the chief ministers held that the edict had already been issued and would not be reversed; they only halted the posthumous offices for Duozhuo and the others.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed heartily, but the chief ministers refused to reverse an edict already issued and merely withheld posthumous honors from Duozhuo and his fellows.

sentences.zh: 十一月，戊申朔，以姚元之為中書令。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on the first day of the month wushen, Yao Chongzhi was made director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on the new moon of wushen, Yao Yuanzhi was appointed Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，葬孝和皇帝於定陵，廟號中宗。

translations.literal: On the day yiyou, Emperor Xiaohé was buried at Dingling; his temple name was Zhongzong.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou day, Emperor Xiaohé was buried at Dingling with the temple name Zhongzong.

sentences.zh: 朝議以韋後有罪，不應祔葬。

translations.literal: Court discussion held that Empress Wei was guilty and ought not to be buried alongside him.
translations.idiomatic: The court held that guilty Empress Wei should not share his tomb.

sentences.zh: 追謚故英王妃趙氏曰和思順聖皇后，求其瘞，莫有知者，乃以禕衣招魂，覆以夷衾，祔葬定陵。

translations.literal: The former Princess of Ying, née Zhao, was posthumously titled Empress Hesishun Sheng; they sought her burial place but none knew it, so they summoned her soul with a single garment, covered it with a plain quilt, and enshrined her at Dingling.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhongzong's first consort, Lady Zhao of Ying, was posthumously named Empress Hesishun Sheng; no one knew where she lay, so a garment was used to summon her spirit, wrapped in a plain quilt, and she was buried beside him at Dingling.

sentences.zh: 壬子，侍中韋安石罷為太子少保，左僕射、同中書門下三呂蘇瑰罷為少傅。

translations.literal: On the day renzi, chief minister Wei Anshi was removed to be grand protector of the heir apparent; left vice director of the Department of State Affairs and fellow chief minister Su Gui was removed to be junior mentor.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi day, Wei Anshi was demoted from chief minister to Grand Protector of the Heir Apparent, and Su Gui from Left Vice Director and chief minister to Junior Mentor.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，追復裴炎官爵。

translations.literal: On the day jiayin, Pei Yan's offices and titles were posthumously restored.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin day, Pei Yan's offices and titles were posthumously restored.

sentences.zh: 初，裴胄先自嶺南逃歸，復杖一百，徙北庭。

translations.literal: Earlier, Pei Zhouxian had fled back from Lingnan, was again beaten one hundred strokes, and was banished to Beiting.
translations.idiomatic: Years before, Pei Zhouxian had escaped from exile in Lingnan, was flogged a hundred strokes, and sent to Beiting.

sentences.zh: 至徙所，殖貨任俠，常遣客言□都下事。

translations.literal: At his place of banishment he amassed wealth and played the knight-errant, often sending agents to report on affairs in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: At his place of exile he amassed wealth and played the chivalrous patron, often sending agents to report on affairs in the capital.

sentences.zh: 武後之誅流人也，胄先先知之，逃奔胡中；

translations.literal: When Empress Wu was about to execute the exiles, Zhouxian learned of it beforehand and fled among the barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Wu moved to execute the exiles, Zhouxian learned of it in advance and fled to the nomad lands.

sentences.zh: 北庭都護追獲，囚之以聞。

translations.literal: The protector of Beiting pursued and captured him, imprisoned him, and reported upward.
translations.idiomatic: The Beiting protector pursued him, captured him, and reported to the court.

sentences.zh: 使者至，流人盡死，胄先以待報未殺。

translations.literal: When the envoy arrived, the exiles were all killed; Zhouxian alone was not killed, awaiting further report.
translations.idiomatic: When the envoy arrived, every exile was killed; Zhouxian alone was spared, pending further orders.

sentences.zh: 既而武後下制安撫流人，有未死者悉放還，胄先由是得歸。

translations.literal: Soon after, Empress Wu issued an edict to reassure the exiles; any not yet dead were all released and sent home, and Zhouxian thereby returned.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu then issued an edict of clemency; survivors were released, and Zhouxian came home.

sentences.zh: 至是求炎後，獨胄先在，拜詹事丞。

translations.literal: Now they sought descendants of Pei Yan; only Zhouxian remained, and he was appointed vice director of the Household Administration of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When the court sought Pei Yan's heirs, only Zhouxian survived and was made Vice Director of the Heir Apparent's Household.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，追復王同皎官爵。

translations.literal: On the day renxu, Wang Tongjiao's offices and titles were posthumously restored.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu day, Wang Tongjiao's offices and titles were posthumously restored.

sentences.zh: 庚午，許文貞公蘇瑰薨。

translations.literal: On the day gengwu, Duke Wen Zhen Su Gui died.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu day, Duke Wen Zhen Su Gui died.

sentences.zh: 制起復其子頲為工部侍郎，頲固辭。

translations.literal: An edict recalled his son Ting from mourning to serve as vice minister of works; Ting firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: An edict recalled his son Ting from mourning to serve as Vice Minister of Works; Ting firmly refused.

sentences.zh: 上使李日知諭旨，日知終坐不言而還，奏曰：「臣見其哀毀，不忍發言，恐其隕絕。」

translations.literal: The emperor sent Li Rizhi to convey the order; Rizhi in the end sat without speaking and returned, memorializing: "I saw his grief and devastation and could not bear to speak, fearing he would collapse and die."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Li Rizhi to convey the order; Rizhi sat in silence and returned, reporting: "His grief was so overwhelming I dared not speak—for fear he would die of it."

sentences.zh: 上乃聽其終制。

translations.literal: The emperor then allowed him to complete his mourning.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor let him complete his mourning.

sentences.zh: 十二月，癸未，上以二女西城、隆昌公主為女官，以資天皇天後之福，仍欲於京城西造觀。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on the day guiwei, the emperor made his two daughters, the Princesses of Xicheng and Longchang, female officials [of the Daoist church] to add to the blessings of the Heavenly Emperor and Heavenly Empress, and also wished to build an abbey west of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on guiwei day, the emperor made his daughters, the Princesses of Xicheng and Longchang, Daoist nuns to win blessings for his parents and planned to build an abbey west of the capital.

sentences.zh: 諫議大夫寧原悌上言，以為：「先朝悖逆庶人以愛女驕盈而及禍，新都、宜城以庶孽抑損而獲全。

translations.literal: Remonstrance official Ning Yuantie submitted a memorial, arguing: "In the previous reign the rebellious commoner perished because he spoiled his beloved daughter; Xindu and Yicheng, as lesser-born daughters who were kept in check, survived intact.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance Official Ning Yuantie argued: "The rebel prince of the last reign was ruined by indulging his favorite daughter; Princesses Xindu and Yicheng survived because they were kept in check as lesser-born daughters.

sentences.zh: 又釋、道二家皆以清淨為本，不當廣營寺觀，勞人費財。

translations.literal: Moreover, both Buddhism and Daoism take purity and stillness as their foundation; one ought not broadly to build temples and abbeys, exhausting the people and wasting wealth.
translations.idiomatic: Buddhism and Daoism alike prize purity and restraint; lavish temples waste the people's labor and the treasury's coin.

sentences.zh: 梁武致敗於前，先帝取災於後，殷鑒不遠。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang brought defeat upon himself before; the late emperor met disaster after—recent warnings are not far to seek.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang ruined his state with such excess; our late emperor suffered for the same folly—the lesson is recent.

sentences.zh: 今二公主入道，將為之置觀，不宜過為崇麗，取謗四方。

translations.literal: Now the two princesses enter the Way and an abbey will be built for them; it is not fitting to make it excessively grand and splendid, inviting censure from all quarters.
translations.idiomatic: If the two princesses take vows and an abbey is built for them, it should not be so grand as to draw scandal from every quarter.

sentences.zh: 又，先朝所親狎諸僧，尚在左右，宜加屏斥。」

translations.literal: Moreover, the monks whom the previous reign favored and kept close are still at hand; they ought to be removed and expelled."
translations.idiomatic: The monks the late emperor favored still linger at court and should be dismissed."

sentences.zh: 上覽而善之。

translations.literal: The emperor read it and approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read the memorial and approved.

sentences.zh: 宦者閭興貴以事屬長安令李朝隱，朝隱繫於獄。

translations.literal: The eunuch Lü Xinggui had a matter that fell under the jurisdiction of the Chang'an magistrate Li Chaoyin; Chaoyin imprisoned him.
translations.idiomatic: When the eunuch Lü Xinggui tried to pull rank on Chang'an Magistrate Li Chaoyin, Chaoyin threw him in jail.

sentences.zh: 上聞之，召見朝隱，勞之曰：「卿為赤縣令，能如此，朕復何憂！」

translations.literal: When the emperor heard of it, he summoned Chaoyin and comforted him, saying, "As magistrate of the imperial county, if you can act thus, what have I to worry about!"
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard, he summoned Chaoyin and said, "As magistrate of the imperial county, if you can act thus, what have I to fear!"

sentences.zh: 因御承天門，集百官及諸州朝集使，宣示以朝隱所為，且下制稱「宦官遇寬柔之代，必弄威權。

translations.literal: He then went out to the Chengtian Gate, assembled the officials and the provincial envoys gathered for court, proclaimed what Chaoyin had done, and issued an edict stating, "When eunuchs meet a lenient age, they are sure to wield power.
translations.idiomatic: He then appeared at Chengtian Gate, assembled officials and provincial envoys, proclaimed Chaoyin's conduct, and issued an edict: "In lenient times eunuchs always seize power.

sentences.zh: 朕覽前載，每所歎息。

translations.literal: When I read the records of the past, I sigh each time.
translations.idiomatic: Reading history, I sigh every time.

sentences.zh: 能副朕意，實在斯人，可加一階為太中大夫，賜中上考及絹百匹。」

translations.literal: To fulfill my intent—truly it is this man; he may be promoted one rank to Grand Masters of Palace Attendance, and granted a middle-upper evaluation and one hundred bolts of silk."
translations.idiomatic: The man who fulfills my intent is before you: promote him one rank to Grand Master of Palace Attendance, grant him a middle-upper evaluation, and award a hundred bolts of silk."

sentences.zh: 壬辰，奚、□犯塞，掠漁陽、雍奴，出盧龍塞而去。

translations.literal: On the day renchen, the Xi and Khitan raided the frontier, plundered Yuyang and Yongnu, and withdrew through Lulong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen day, Xi and Khitan forces raided the frontier, plundered Yuyang and Yongnu, and withdrew through Lulong Pass.

sentences.zh: 幽州都督薛訥追擊之，弗克。

translations.literal: Xue Ne, regional commander of Youzhou, pursued them but could not overcome them.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhou Commander Xue Ne pursued them but failed to defeat them.

sentences.zh: 舊制，三品以上官冊授，五品以上制授，六品以下敕授，皆委尚書省奏擬，文屬吏部，武屬兵部，尚書曰中銓，侍郎曰東西銓。

translations.literal: By old regulation, officials of the third rank and above were appointed by imperial patent, fifth rank and above by edict, sixth rank and below by decree; all were entrusted to the Department of State Affairs for memorial nomination. Civil posts belonged to the Ministry of Personnel, military to the Ministry of War; the minister was called the central selection, the vice ministers the eastern and western selection.
translations.idiomatic: By established rule, third-rank officials and above received patent appointments, fifth-rank and above edict appointments, sixth-rank and below decree appointments—all nominated through the Department of State Affairs. Civil posts fell to the Ministry of Personnel, military to the Ministry of War; the minister headed the central selection board, the vice ministers the eastern and western boards.

sentences.zh: 中宗之末，嬖倖用事，選舉混淆，無復綱紀。

translations.literal: At the end of Zhongzong's reign, favorites held power; selections were confused and there was no longer any order.
translations.idiomatic: By the end of Zhongzong's reign, favorites had corrupted appointments beyond recognition.

sentences.zh: 至是，以宋璟為吏部尚書，李乂、盧從願為侍郎，皆不畏強禦，請謁路絕。

translations.literal: Now Song Jing was made minister of personnel, Li Yi and Lu Congyuan vice ministers; none feared the powerful, and the road of private petitions was cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Now Song Jing headed the Ministry of Personnel with Li Yi and Lu Congyuan as vice ministers; they feared no power, and favor-seeking at their door ended.

sentences.zh: 集者萬餘人，留者三銓不過二千，人服其公。

translations.literal: Those who gathered numbered more than ten thousand; those retained by the three selection boards did not exceed two thousand, and the people admired their fairness.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten thousand candidates presented themselves; the three boards retained fewer than two thousand, and the realm admired their integrity.

sentences.zh: 以姚元之為兵部尚書，陸象先、盧懷慎為侍郎，武選亦治。

translations.literal: Yao Chongzhi was made minister of war, Lu Xiangxian and Lu Huaiqian vice ministers, and military selection was also put in order.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Yuanzhi headed the Ministry of War with Lu Xiangxian and Lu Huaiqian as vice ministers, and military appointments were brought to order as well.

sentences.zh: 從願，承慶之族子；

translations.literal: Congyuan was a clansman of Chengqing.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Congyuan was a kinsman of Chengqing.

sentences.zh: 象先，元方之子也。

translations.literal: Xiangxian was the son of Yuanfang.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xiangxian was Lu Yuanfang's son.

sentences.zh: 侍御史蒿城倪若水，奏彈國子祭酒祝欽明、司業郭山惲亂常改作，希旨病君；

translations.literal: Censor Ni Ruoshui of Gaocheng memorialized, impeaching Chancellor of the Imperial Academy Zhu Qinming and Vice-Chancellor Guo Shanyun for overturning the constant order and altering institutions, currying favor by slandering the ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Ni Ruoshui, a censor from Gaocheng, impeached Zhu Qinming, Chancellor of the Imperial Academy, and Guo Shanyun, his vice-chancellor, for subverting orthodoxy and reshaping institutions to please the throne by maligning their sovereign.

sentences.zh: 於是左授欽明饒州刺史，山惲括州長史。

translations.literal: Thereupon Zhu Qinming was demoted to Prefect of Raozhou, and Guo Shanyun to Senior Administrator of Kuozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Qinming was demoted to prefect of Raozhou, and Guo Shanyun to senior administrator of Kuozhou.

sentences.zh: 侍御史楊孚，彈糾不避權貴，權貴毀之。

translations.literal: Censor Yang Fu impeached and investigated without avoiding the powerful and noble; the powerful and noble slandered him.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Yang Fu investigated without fear of the mighty, and the mighty in turn defamed him.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「鷹搏狡兔，須急救之，不爾必反為所噬。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "When a hawk strikes a cunning hare, one must rush to rescue it at once; otherwise it will surely in turn be devoured by it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "When a hawk closes on a cunning hare, it must be rescued at once—otherwise the hawk itself will be torn apart.

sentences.zh: 御史繩奸慝亦然。

translations.literal: It is the same when censors bind up the wicked and villainous.
translations.idiomatic: The same is true when censors pursue treachery and villainy.

sentences.zh: 敬非人主保衛之，則亦為奸慝所噬矣。」

translations.literal: Were it not for the sovereign's protection, they too would be devoured by the wicked and villainous."
translations.idiomatic: Without the sovereign's protection, they too would be consumed by those very villains."

sentences.zh: 孚，隋文帝之侄孫也。

translations.literal: Yang Fu was a grand-nephew of Emperor Wen of Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Fu was a grand-nephew of Emperor Wen of Sui.

sentences.zh: 置河西節度、支度、營田等使，領涼、甘、肅、伊、瓜、沙、西七州，治涼州。

translations.literal: The posts of Hexi military commissioner, supply commissioner, garrison-farming commissioner, and the like were established, governing the seven prefectures of Liang, Gan, Su, Yi, Gua, Sha, and Xi, with the seat at Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Posts of Hexi military commissioner, supply commissioner, and garrison-farming commissioner were created, governing Liang, Gan, Su, Yi, Gua, Sha, and Xi—seven prefectures—with headquarters at Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 姚州群蠻，先附吐蕃，攝監察御史李知古請發兵擊之；

translations.literal: The tribal peoples of Yaozhou had earlier submitted to Tibet; Acting Censor Li Zhigu requested that troops be sent to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: The tribal peoples of Yaozhou had earlier submitted to Tibet; Li Zhigu, acting censor, asked that troops be sent against them.

sentences.zh: 既降，又請築城，列置州縣，重稅之。

translations.literal: After they had surrendered, he again requested to build fortifications, establish prefectures and counties in array, and levy heavy taxes.
translations.idiomatic: Once they had submitted, he asked again to build fortifications, set up prefectures and counties, and impose heavy taxes.

sentences.zh: 黃門侍郎徐堅以為不可；

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Yellow Gate Xu Jian held that this should not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Jian, Vice Director of the Yellow Gate, argued against it.

sentences.zh: 不從。

translations.literal: The emperor did not follow his advice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not heed him.

sentences.zh: 知古發劍南兵築城，因欲誅其豪傑，掠子女為奴婢。

translations.literal: Zhigu mobilized Jiannan troops to build the fortifications, intending thereby to execute their leading men and seize sons and daughters as slaves and maidservants.
translations.idiomatic: Zhigu raised troops from Jiannan to build the fortifications, intending to kill the tribal leaders and carry off their sons and daughters as slaves.

sentences.zh: 群蠻怨怨，蠻酋傍名引吐蕃攻知古，殺之，以其屍祭天，由是姚、巂路絕，連年不通。

translations.literal: The tribes were filled with resentment; the tribal chief Bangming led Tibet to attack Zhigu and killed him, offering his corpse in sacrifice to Heaven; thereby the routes through Yao and Xi were cut off, and for years there was no communication.
translations.idiomatic: The tribes seethed with resentment. Their chief Bangming brought in the Tibetans, attacked Zhigu, and killed him, offering his body in sacrifice to Heaven. From that time the roads through Yao and Xi were severed for years.

sentences.zh: 安西都護張玄表侵掠吐蕃北境，吐蕃雖怨而未絕和親，乃賂鄯州都督楊矩，請河西九曲之地以為公主湯沐邑；

translations.literal: Protector-General of Anxi Zhang Xuanbiao raided and plundered Tibet's northern frontier; though Tibet resented this, it had not yet broken off the marriage alliance, and so bribed Prefect of Shanzhou Yang Ju, requesting the land of the Nine Bends west of the He River as a fief for the princess's bath-and-maintenance estate.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xuanbiao, Protector-General of Anxi, raided Tibet's northern borderlands. The Tibetans resented it but had not yet broken the marriage alliance; instead they bribed Yang Ju, prefect of Shanzhou, asking for the Nine Bends west of the Yellow River as a maintenance fief for the princess.

sentences.zh: 矩奏與之。

translations.literal: Yang Ju memorialized recommending that it be granted.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Ju memorialized recommending the grant, and it was given.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，癸丑，突厥可汗默啜遣使請和；

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on the day guichou, Khaghan Moqu of the Turks sent envoys requesting peace.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, in the first month, on guichou, Moqu, khaghan of the Turks, sent envoys to sue for peace.

sentences.zh: 許之。

translations.literal: The emperor granted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 己未，以太僕卿郭元振、中書侍郎張說並同平章事。

translations.literal: On the day jiwei, Grand Master of the Imperial Stud Guo Yuanzhen and Vice Director of the Secretariat Zhang Shuo were both appointed Grand Councilors of State.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei, Guo Yuanzhen, Grand Master of the Imperial Stud, and Zhang Shuo, Vice Director of the Secretariat, were both made Grand Councilors of State.

sentences.zh: 以溫王重茂為襄王，充集州刺史，遣中郎將將兵五百就防之。

translations.literal: Prince Wen Zhongmao was made Prince Xiang, appointed Prefect of Jizhou, and a battalion commander was dispatched with five hundred troops to guard him on site.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Wen Zhongmao was renamed Prince Xiang, made prefect of Jizhou, and a battalion commander was sent with five hundred men to keep watch over him.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，追立妃劉氏曰肅明皇后，陵曰惠陵；

translations.literal: On the day yichou, Consort Liu was posthumously elevated as Empress Suming, her tomb named Huiling.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou, Consort Liu was posthumously enthroned as Empress Suming; her tomb was called Huiling.

sentences.zh: 德妃竇氏曰昭成皇后，陵曰靖陵。

translations.literal: Virtuous Consort Dou was named Empress Zhaocheng, her tomb Jingling.
translations.idiomatic: Virtuous Consort Dou was named Empress Zhaocheng; her tomb was called Jingling.

sentences.zh: 皆招魂葬於東都城南，立廟京師，號儀坤廟。

translations.literal: Both were given soul-summoning burials south of the Eastern Capital, and temples were established in the capital, called the Yikun Shrine.
translations.idiomatic: Both were given soul-summoning burials south of the Eastern Capital; shrines were raised in the capital and named the Yikun Shrine.

sentences.zh: 竇氏，太子之母也。

translations.literal: Dou was the crown prince's mother.
translations.idiomatic: Dou was the crown prince's mother.

sentences.zh: 太平公主與益州長史竇懷貞等結為朋黨，欲以危太子，使其婿唐晙邀韋安石至其第，安石固辭不往。

translations.literal: Princess Taiping formed a faction with Senior Administrator of Yizhou Dou Huaizhen and others, seeking to endanger the crown prince; she had her son-in-law Tang Jun invite Wei Anshi to her residence, but Anshi steadfastly declined and did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Taiping joined in faction with Dou Huaizhen, senior administrator of Yizhou, and others, plotting to undermine the crown prince. She had her son-in-law Tang Jun invite Wei Anshi to her house, but Anshi firmly refused and would not go.

sentences.zh: 上嘗密召安石，謂曰：「聞朝廷皆傾心東宮，卿宜察之。」

translations.literal: The emperor once secretly summoned Anshi and said: "I hear that the entire court inclines its heart toward the Eastern Palace—you should investigate this."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once summoned Anshi in secret and said, "I hear the whole court is turning toward the Eastern Palace. You should look into this."

sentences.zh: 對曰：「陛下安得亡國之言！

translations.literal: He replied: "How can Your Majesty speak words that would ruin the state!
translations.idiomatic: Anshi answered, "How can Your Majesty utter words that would destroy the realm!

sentences.zh: 此必太平之謀耳。

translations.literal: This must surely be Princess Taiping's plot.
translations.idiomatic: This must be Princess Taiping's doing.

sentences.zh: 太子有功於社稷，仁明孝友，天下所知，願陛下無惑讒言。」

translations.literal: The crown prince has rendered service to the altars of soil and grain; he is benevolent, enlightened, filial, and brotherly—the realm knows this. I pray Your Majesty not be misled by slander."
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince has served the altars of state with merit; his benevolence, wisdom, filial piety, and brotherly devotion are known to all under Heaven. I beg Your Majesty not to be swayed by calumny."

sentences.zh: 上瞿然曰：「朕知之矣，卿勿言。」

translations.literal: The emperor started in alarm and said: "I understand now—you say no more."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor started and said, "I understand. Say no more."

sentences.zh: 時公主在簾下竊聽之，以飛語陷安石，欲收按之，賴郭元振救之，得免。

translations.literal: At that time the princess was behind the curtain secretly listening; she spread malicious rumors to frame Anshi and sought to arrest and investigate him, but thanks to Guo Yuanzhen's rescue he escaped punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The princess was then eavesdropping from behind the curtain. She spread slander to entrap Anshi and tried to have him arrested and prosecuted, but Guo Yuanzhen intervened and he was spared.

sentences.zh: 公主又嘗乘輦邀宰相於光范門內，諷以易置東宮，眾皆失色，宋璟抗言曰：「東宮有大功於天下，真宗廟社稷之主，公主奈何忽有此議！」

translations.literal: The princess also once rode in her palanquin to invite the chief ministers inside the Guangfan Gate, implying that the Eastern Palace might be replaced; all turned pale. Song Jing spoke boldly: "The Eastern Palace has rendered great service to the realm—he is the true lord of the dynastic temples and altars. How can Your Highness suddenly raise such a proposal!"
translations.idiomatic: The princess also once rode in her carriage to summon the chief ministers inside the Guangfan Gate, hinting that the Eastern Palace might be replaced. All paled. Song Jing spoke up boldly: "The Eastern Palace has won great merit for the realm and is the true heir to the ancestral temples. How can Your Highness suddenly broach such a thing!"

sentences.zh: 璟與姚元之密言於上曰：「宋王陛下之元子，豳王高宗之長孫，太平公主交構其間，將使東宮不安。

translations.literal: Song Jing and Yao Yuanzhi spoke secretly to the emperor: "Prince Song is Your Majesty's eldest son; Prince Bin is Empress Gaozong's eldest grandson. Princess Taiping is weaving intrigue between them, which will unsettle the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Song Jing and Yao Yuanzhi spoke privately to the emperor: "Prince Song is Your Majesty's eldest son; Prince Bin is the eldest grandson of Emperor Gaozong. Princess Taiping is stirring trouble between them and will make the Eastern Palace insecure.

sentences.zh: 請出宋王及豳王皆為刺史，罷岐、薛二王左、右羽林，使為左、右率以事太子。

translations.literal: We request that Princes Song and Bin both be sent out as prefects, that Princes Qi and Xue be removed from the Left and Right Forest Armies and made Left and Right Guard Commanders to serve the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: We ask that Princes Song and Bin be sent out as prefects, and that Princes Qi and Xue be removed from command of the Left and Right Forest Armies and made Left and Right Guard Commanders to attend the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 太平公主請與武攸暨皆於東都安置。」

translations.literal: As for Princess Taiping, we request that she and Wu Youji both be resettled at the Eastern Capital."
translations.idiomatic: We also ask that Princess Taiping and Wu Youji both be relocated to the Eastern Capital."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「朕更無兄弟，惟太平一妹，豈可遠置東都！

translations.literal: The emperor said: "I have no brothers left—only my sister Taiping. How can I banish her to the Eastern Capital!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I have no brothers left—only my sister Taiping. How can I send her far off to the Eastern Capital!

sentences.zh: 諸王惟卿所處。」

translations.literal: As for the princes, dispose of them as you see fit."
translations.idiomatic: As for the princes, do with them as you judge best."

sentences.zh: 乃先下制云：「諸王、駙馬自今毋得典禁兵，見任者皆改它宮。」

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict was first promulgated stating: "From this day forward, princes and imperial sons-in-law shall not command the forbidden armies; those currently holding such posts shall all be transferred to other offices."
translations.idiomatic: An edict was then issued first: "Henceforth princes and imperial sons-in-law may not hold command of the forbidden armies; those now in such posts shall all be reassigned."

sentences.zh: 頃之，上謂侍臣曰：「術者言於五日當有急兵入宮，卿等為朕備之。」

translations.literal: Shortly afterward the emperor told his attendants: "A diviner says that within five days armed assailants will enter the palace—you must prepare for this on my behalf."
translations.idiomatic: Before long the emperor told his attendants, "A diviner says that within five days armed men will enter the palace. Prepare for this on my behalf."

sentences.zh: 張說曰：「此必讒人欲離間東宮。

translations.literal: Zhang Shuo said: "This must be slanderers seeking to drive a wedge between Your Majesty and the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shuo said, "This must be the work of slanderers trying to estrange Your Majesty from the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 願陛下使太子監國，則流言自息矣。」

translations.literal: I pray Your Majesty appoint the crown prince to supervise the state—then the idle rumors will cease of themselves."
translations.idiomatic: Let Your Majesty put the crown prince in charge of the realm, and the rumors will die away of themselves."

sentences.zh: 姚元之曰：「張說所言，社稷之至計也。」

translations.literal: Yao Yuanzhi said: "What Zhang Shuo proposes is the supreme strategy for the altars of soil and grain."
translations.idiomatic: Yao Yuanzhi said, "What Zhang Shuo advises is the highest policy for the altars of state."

sentences.zh: 上悅。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased.

sentences.zh: 二月，丙子朔，以宋王成器為同州刺史，豳王守禮為豳州刺史，左羽林大將軍岐王隆范為左衛率，右羽林大將軍薛王隆業為右衛率；

translations.literal: In the second month, on the first day of the cycle (bingzi), Prince Song Chengqi was made Prefect of Tongzhou, Prince Bin Shouli Prefect of Binzhou, Grand General of the Left Forest Army Prince Qi Longfan was made Left Guard Commander, and Grand General of the Right Forest Army Prince Xue Longye Right Guard Commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on the first day, bingzi, Prince Song Chengqi was made prefect of Tongzhou; Prince Bin Shouli, prefect of Binzhou; Prince Qi Longfan, Grand General of the Left Forest Army, was made Left Guard Commander; and Prince Xue Longye, Grand General of the Right Forest Army, was made Right Guard Commander.

sentences.zh: 太平公主蒲州安置。

translations.literal: Princess Taiping was resettled at Puzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Taiping was relocated to Puzhou.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，命太子監國，六品以下除官及徒罪以下，並取太子處分。

translations.literal: On the day dingchou, the crown prince was ordered to supervise the state; appointments and removals of officials of the sixth rank and below, as well as punishments up to penal servitude, were all left to the crown prince's discretion.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou, the crown prince was put in charge of the realm. Appointments and dismissals of officials of the sixth rank and below, and punishments up to penal servitude, were all entrusted to his judgment.

sentences.zh: 殿中侍御史崔蒞、太子中允薛照素言於上曰：「斜封官皆先帝所除，恩命已布，姚元之等建議，一朝盡奪之，彰先帝之過，為陛下招怨。

translations.literal: Palace censor Cui Li and crown prince attendant Xue Zhaosu said to the emperor: "The irregular appointees were all installed by the late emperor; the gracious orders have already been promulgated. Yao Yuanzhi and others proposed that they all be stripped away in a single morning, exposing the late emperor's faults and drawing resentment upon Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Censor Cui Li and Crown Prince Attendant Xue Zhaosu told the emperor: "The slant-seal appointees were all installed by the late emperor, and his grace has already been proclaimed. To strip them all away at once, as Yao Yuanzhi urged, exposes the late emperor's errors and wins Your Majesty resentment.

sentences.zh: 今眾口沸騰，遍於海內，恐生非常之變。」

translations.literal: Now mouths boil everywhere throughout the realm; I fear an extraordinary upheaval may arise."
translations.idiomatic: Talk is boiling across the realm; I fear some extraordinary upheaval may follow."

sentences.zh: 太平公主亦言之，上以為然。

translations.literal: Princess Taiping also spoke thus, and the emperor thought it right.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Taiping said the same, and the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，制：「諸緣斜封別敕授官，先停任者，並量材敘用。」

translations.literal: On the day wuyin, an edict stated: "All who received office through irregular slant-seal special edicts and were previously suspended shall be reassigned according to their talents."
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin day an edict declared: "All officials appointed by irregular slant-seal edicts who were previously suspended shall be reassigned according to merit."

sentences.zh: 太平公主聞姚元之、宋璟之謀，大怒，以讓太子。

translations.literal: When Princess Taiping heard of Yao Yuanzhi's and Song Jing's plot, she was greatly angered and reproached the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: When Princess Taiping learned of Yao Yuanzhi's and Song Jing's plan, she flew into a rage and rebuked the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 太子懼，奏元之、璟離間姑、兄，請從極法。

translations.literal: The crown prince, in fear, memorialized that Yuanzhi and Jing had driven a wedge between aunt and brother and requested the utmost penalty.
translations.idiomatic: Frightened, the crown prince memorialized that Yuanzhi and Jing had estranged his aunt and brother and asked that they be punished to the full extent of the law.

sentences.zh: 甲申，貶元之為申州刺史，璟為楚州刺史。

translations.literal: On the day jiashen, Yuanzhi was demoted to Prefect of Shenzhou and Jing to Prefect of Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen day, Yuanzhi was demoted to prefect of Shenzhou and Jing to prefect of Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，宋王、豳王亦寢刺史之命。

translations.literal: On the day bingxu, the orders making Princes Song and Bin prefects were also suspended.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu day, the orders sending Princes Song and Bin out as prefects were also suspended.

sentences.zh: 中書舍人、參知機務劉幽求罷為戶部尚書；

translations.literal: Secretariat drafter and participant in state affairs Liu Youqiu was removed to be minister of revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat Drafter Liu Youqiu, who had shared in governing, was demoted to Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 以太子少保韋安石為侍中。

translations.literal: Grand Protector of the Heir Apparent Wei Anshi was made chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Protector of the Heir Apparent Wei Anshi was made chief minister.

sentences.zh: 安石與李日知代姚、宋為政，自是綱紀紊亂，復如景龍之世矣。

translations.literal: Anshi and Li Rizhi replaced Yao and Song in governing; from this time order was disordered again, as in the Jinglong era.
translations.idiomatic: Anshi and Li Rizhi replaced Yao and Song at the helm; from then on discipline collapsed again, as in the Jinglong years.

sentences.zh: 前右率府鎧曹參軍柳澤上疏，以為：「斜封官皆因僕妾汲引，豈出孝和之意！

translations.literal: Former armor-office clerk of the Right Guard Office Liu Ze submitted a memorial, arguing: "The irregular appointees all came in through maidservants' pull—how could that have been Emperor Xiaohé's intent!
translations.idiomatic: Former armor-office clerk of the Right Guard Office, Liu Ze, argued in a memorial: "Those slant-seal officials all entered through maidservants' favor—how could that have been Emperor Xiaohé's intent!

sentences.zh: 陛下一切黜之，天下莫不稱明。

translations.literal: Your Majesty dismissed them all at once, and none under Heaven failed to call it enlightened.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty dismissed them all at once, and the realm hailed your wisdom.

sentences.zh: 一旦忽盡收斜，善惡不安，反覆相攻，何陛下政令之不一也！

translations.literal: Yet in a single morning you suddenly recall all the irregular appointees; good and evil are unsettled, attack and counterattack each other—how can Your Majesty's orders be so inconsistent!
translations.idiomatic: Yet in a single morning you recall them all—good and evil alike are unsettled, and factions attack one another. How can Your Majesty's orders be so inconsistent!

sentences.zh: 議者咸稱太平公主令胡僧慧范曲引此曹，誑誤陛下。

translations.literal: Commentators all say Princess Taiping had the barbarian monk Huifan improperly draw in this crowd and mislead Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone says Princess Taiping had the monk Huifan draw this crowd back in and mislead Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 臣恐積小成大，為禍不細。」

translations.literal: I fear that small things will accumulate into great ones and the harm will not be slight."
translations.idiomatic: I fear small errors will grow into great disaster."

sentences.zh: 上弗聽。

translations.literal: The emperor did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 澤，亨之孫也。

translations.literal: Ze was the grandson of Hen.
translations.idiomatic: Ze was the grandson of Liu Hen.

sentences.zh: 左、右萬騎與左右羽林為北門四軍，使葛福順等將之。

translations.literal: The left and right Ten Thousand Riders together with the left and right Imperial Guard formed the four Northern Gate armies, with Ge Fushun and others commanding them.
translations.idiomatic: The left and right Ten Thousand Riders and the left and right Imperial Guard formed the four Northern Gate armies under Ge Fushun and others.

sentences.zh: 三月，以宋王成器女為金山公主，許嫁突厥默啜。

translations.literal: In the third month, the daughter of Prince Song Chengqi was made Princess Jinshan, betrothed to Khaghan Moqu of the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, Prince Song Chengqi's daughter was made Princess Jinshan and betrothed to Moqu, khaghan of the Turks.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，甲申，宋王成器讓司徒；

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on the day jiashen, Prince Song Chengqi yielded the post of Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer, on jiashen day, Prince Song Chengqi resigned as Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 許之，以為太子賓客。

translations.literal: The request was granted; he was made guest of the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: The request was granted, and he was made Guest of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 以韋安石為中書令。

translations.literal: Wei Anshi was made director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Anshi was made Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 上召群臣三品以上，謂曰：「朕素懷澹泊，不以萬乘為貴，曩為皇嗣，又為皇太弟，皆辭不處。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned officials of the third rank and above and said: "I have long cherished simplicity and do not regard the ten-thousand-chariot throne as precious; formerly as imperial heir and again as imperial younger brother, I declined both.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned officials of the third rank and above and said, "I have long cherished simplicity and do not prize the throne; as heir and again as imperial younger brother I declined both.

sentences.zh: 今欲傳位太子，何如？」

translations.literal: Now I wish to pass the throne to the crown prince—what do you think?"
translations.idiomatic: Now I wish to pass the throne to the crown prince—what do you think?"

sentences.zh: 群臣莫對。

translations.literal: The officials none replied.
translations.idiomatic: No one answered.

sentences.zh: 太子使右庶子李景伯固辭，不許。

translations.literal: The crown prince sent Right Vice Director Li Jingbo to decline firmly; this was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince sent Right Vice Director Li Jingbo to decline firmly; the emperor would not allow it.

sentences.zh: 殿中侍御史和逢堯附太平公主，言於上曰：「陛下春秋未高，方為四海所依仰，豈得遽爾！」

translations.literal: Palace censor He Fengyao, attached to Princess Taiping, said to the emperor: "Your Majesty's years are not yet advanced, and you are the reliance of all within the four seas—how can you do this so hastily!"
translations.idiomatic: Palace Censor He Fengyao, aligned with Princess Taiping, said, "Your Majesty is not yet old, and the realm still depends on you—how can you act so hastily!"

sentences.zh: 上乃止。

translations.literal: The emperor then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then abandoned the idea.

sentences.zh: 戊子，制：「凡政事皆取太子處分。

translations.literal: On the day wuzi, an edict stated: "All government affairs shall be decided by the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi day an edict declared: "All government affairs shall be decided by the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 其軍旅死刑及五品已上除授，皆先與太子議之，然後以聞。」

translations.literal: Military punishments, death sentences, and appointments and dismissals of the fifth rank and above must first be discussed with the crown prince and then reported."
translations.idiomatic: Military matters, death sentences, and appointments and dismissals of the fifth rank and above must first be discussed with the crown prince before being reported."

sentences.zh: 辛卯，以李日知守侍中。

translations.literal: On the day xinmao, Li Rizhi was appointed acting chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao day, Li Rizhi was appointed acting chief minister.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，赦天下。

translations.literal: On the day renyin, there was a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin day there was a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 五月，太子請讓位於宋王成器；

translations.literal: In the fifth month, the crown prince requested to yield the throne to Prince Song Chengqi.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, the crown prince asked to yield the throne to Prince Song Chengqi.

sentences.zh: 不許。

translations.literal: This was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: The request was denied.

sentences.zh: 請召太平公主還京師：許之。

translations.literal: He requested that Princess Taiping be recalled to the capital; this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that Princess Taiping be recalled to the capital; this was granted.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，制：「則天皇后父母墳仍舊為昊陵、順陵，量置官屬。」

translations.literal: On the day gengxu, an edict stated: "The tombs of Empress Wu's parents shall again be named Haoling and Shunling, with officials appointed in due measure."
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu day an edict declared: "The tombs of Empress Wu's parents shall again be Haoling and Shunling, with officials appointed in due measure."

sentences.zh: 太平公主為武攸暨請之也。

translations.literal: Princess Taiping had requested this on behalf of Wu Youji.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Taiping had requested this for Wu Youji.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，更以西城為金仙公主，隆昌為玉真公主，各為之造觀，逼奪民居甚多，用功數百萬。

translations.literal: On the day xinyou, the Princess of Xicheng was renamed Princess Jinxian and the Princess of Longchang Princess Yuzhen; an abbey was built for each, seizing many commoners' dwellings and costing millions in labor.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou day the Princess of Xicheng was renamed Princess Jinxian and the Princess of Longchang Princess Yuzhen; an abbey was built for each, displacing many households at a cost of millions.

sentences.zh: 右散騎常侍魏知古、黃門侍郎李乂諫，皆不聽。

translations.literal: Right Regular Attendant Wei Zhigu and Vice Director of the Yellow Gate Li Yi remonstrated; both were ignored.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhigu, Right Regular Attendant, and Li Yi, Vice Director of the Yellow Gate, remonstrated; the emperor ignored them both.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，殿中監竇懷貞為御史大夫、同平章事。

translations.literal: On the day renxu, Palace Supervisor Dou Huaizhen was made censor-in-chief and Grand Councilor of State.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu day, Palace Supervisor Dou Huaizhen was made Censor-in-Chief and Grand Councilor of State.

sentences.zh: 僧慧范恃太平公主勢，逼奪民產，御史大夫薛謙光與殿中侍御史慕容珣奏彈之。

translations.literal: The monk Huifan relied on Princess Taiping's power, seizing commoners' property; Censor-in-Chief Xue Qianguang and palace censor Murong Xun memorialized to impeach him.
translations.idiomatic: The monk Huifan, relying on Princess Taiping's power, seized commoners' property; Censor-in-Chief Xue Qianguang and Palace Censor Murong Xun impeached him.

sentences.zh: 公主訴於上，出謙光為岐州刺史。

translations.literal: The princess complained to the emperor, and Qianguang was sent out as Prefect of Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: The princess complained to the emperor, and Qianguang was sent out as prefect of Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 明遣使按察十道，議者以山南所部闊遠，乃分為東西道；

translations.literal: In the Ming era envoys were sent to inspect the ten circuits; commentators held that the Shannan circuit's jurisdiction was too broad and distant, so it was divided into eastern and western circuits.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent envoys to inspect the ten circuits; because Shannan's jurisdiction was too vast, it was divided into eastern and western circuits.

sentences.zh: 又分隴右為河西道。

translations.literal: Longyou was also divided into the Hexi circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Longyou was also split into a Hexi circuit.

sentences.zh: 六月、壬午，又分天下置汴、齊、兗、魏、冀、並、蒲、鄜、涇、秦、益、綿、遂、荊、岐、通、梁、襄、揚、安、淮、越、洪、潭二十四都督，各糾察所部刺史以下善惡，惟洛及近畿州不隸都督府。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on the day renwu, the realm was further divided into twenty-four area commands—Bian, Qi, Yan, Wei, Ji, Bing, Pu, Fu, Jing, Qin, Yi, Mian, Sui, Jing, Qi, Tong, Liang, Xiang, Yang, An, Huai, Yue, Hong, and Tan—each to investigate the good and ill conduct of prefects and below within its jurisdiction; only Luoyang and the nearby capital prefectures were not placed under area commands.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on renwu day, the realm was further divided into twenty-four area commands—Bian, Qi, Yan, Wei, Ji, Bing, Pu, Fu, Jing, Qin, Yi, Mian, Sui, Jing, Qi, Tong, Liang, Xiang, Yang, An, Huai, Yue, Hong, and Tan—each to investigate officials from prefect on down; only Luoyang and the capital prefectures were exempt.

sentences.zh: 太子右庶子李景伯、舍人盧輔等上言：「都督專殺生之柄，權任太重。

translations.literal: Right Vice Director of the Heir Apparent Li Jingbo, Attendant Lu Fu, and others submitted a memorial: "Area commanders hold the power of life and death; their authority is too heavy.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jingbo, Right Vice Director of the Heir Apparent, Lu Fu, Attendant, and others argued: "Area commanders hold the power of life and death—their authority is too great.

sentences.zh: 或用非其人，為害不細。

translations.literal: If the wrong men are used, the harm will not be slight.
translations.idiomatic: If the wrong men are appointed, the harm will be grave.

sentences.zh: 今御史秩卑望重，以時巡察，奸宄自禁。」

translations.literal: Now censors hold low rank but heavy prestige; timely inspection keeps treachery in check.
translations.idiomatic: Censors held modest rank yet real authority; regular inspection kept wrongdoing in check."

sentences.zh: 其後竟罷都督，但置十道按察使而已。

translations.literal: Thereafter the area commanders were abolished; only ten circuit inspecting commissioners remained.
translations.idiomatic: In the end the area commanders were abolished, leaving only ten circuit inspecting commissioners.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，癸巳，追復上官昭容，謚曰惠文。

translations.literal: In autumn, seventh month, guisi, Shangguan Zhaorong was posthumously restored; her posthumous title was Huiwen.
translations.idiomatic: Autumn, seventh month, guisi: Shangguan Zhaorong was posthumously rehabilitated as Huiwen.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，以高祖故宅枯柿復生，赦天下。

translations.literal: On yimao, because the withered persimmon at Gaozu's old residence sprouted anew, an amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao, a dead persimmon at the Founding Emperor's old home leafed out again; the court pardoned the empire.

sentences.zh: 己巳，以右御史大夫解琬為朔方大總管。

translations.literal: On jisi, Right Censor-in-Chief Jie Wan was made Grand Commander of Shuofang.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi, Jie Wan, Right Censor-in-Chief, was made Grand Commander of Shuofang.

sentences.zh: 琬考按三城戍兵，奏減十萬人。

translations.literal: Wan inspected the garrison troops of the three cities and memorialized to cut one hundred thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Jie Wan audited the three frontier garrisons and recommended cutting a hundred thousand troops.

sentences.zh: 庚午，以中書令韋安石為左僕射兼太子賓客、同中書門下三品。

translations.literal: On gengwu, Secretariat Director Wei Anshi was made Left Vice Director of State Affairs, concurrently Crown Prince's Mentor, with third-rank standing.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu, Wei Anshi was named Left Vice Director of State Affairs and Crown Prince's Mentor with third-rank standing.

sentences.zh: 太平公主以安石不附己，故崇以虛名，實去其權也。

translations.literal: Princess Taiping, because Anshi would not join her, honored him with an empty title while stripping his power.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Taiping, finding Wei Anshi unwilling to side with her, gave him hollow honors while removing his real authority.

sentences.zh: 九月，庚辰，以竇懷貞為侍中。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, gengchen, Dou Huaizhen was made Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Ninth month, gengchen: Dou Huaizhen was made Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 懷貞每退朝，必詣太平公主第。

translations.literal: After every court session Huaizhen would go to Princess Taiping's residence.
translations.idiomatic: Each time court adjourned, Dou Huaizhen went straight to the princess's mansion.

sentences.zh: 時修金仙、玉真二觀，群臣多諫，懷貞獨勸成之，身自督役。

translations.literal: At that time the Jin Xian and Yuzhen abbeys were being built; many ministers remonstrated, but Huaizhen alone urged completion and supervised the work.
translations.idiomatic: While the Jin Xian and Yuzhen abbeys were rising, most of the court objected, but Dou Huaizhen alone pressed on and oversaw the labor.

sentences.zh: 時人謂懷貞前為皇后阿{父者}，今為公主邑司。

translations.literal: People said Huaizhen had once been the empress's father-in-law and was now the princess's estate steward.
translations.idiomatic: Wags said he had gone from the empress's father-in-law to the princess's purse-keeper.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，甲辰，上御承天門，引韋安石、郭元振、竇懷貞、李日知、張說宣制，責以「政教多闕，水旱為災，府庫益竭，僚吏日滋；

translations.literal: In winter, tenth month, jiachen, the emperor ascended Chengtian Gate, summoned Wei Anshi, Guo Yuanzhen, Dou Huaizhen, Li Rizhi, and Zhang Yue, and proclaimed a rebuke: 'Government and teaching are full of gaps; flood and drought bring calamity; the treasury empties while officials multiply daily.
translations.idiomatic: Winter, tenth month, jiachen: at Chengtian Gate the emperor had Wei Anshi, Guo Yuanzhen, Dou Huaizhen, Li Rizhi, and Zhang Yue hear a decree of censure: 'Rule is in disarray; flood and drought plague the land; the treasury drains while the bureaucracy swells.

sentences.zh: 雖朕之薄德，亦輔佐非才。

translations.literal: Though Our virtue is slight, Our assistants too lack talent.
translations.idiomatic: If Our own merit is thin, Our ministers have proved no better.

sentences.zh: 安石可左僕射、東都留守，元振可吏部尚書，懷貞可左御史大夫，日知可戶部尚書，說可左丞，並罷政事」。

translations.literal: Anshi shall be Left Vice Director and Eastern Capital Commissioner; Yuanzhen, Minister of Personnel; Huaizhen, Left Censor-in-Chief; Rizhi, Minister of Revenue; Yue, Left Vice Director—all removed from the inner council.'
translations.idiomatic: Wei Anshi to Left Vice Director and Eastern Capital Commissioner; Guo Yuanzhen, Minister of Personnel; Dou Huaizhen, Left Censor-in-Chief; Li Rizhi, Minister of Revenue; Zhang Yue, Left Vice Director—all removed from power.'

sentences.zh: 以吏部尚書劉幽求為侍中，右散騎常侍魏知古為左散騎常侍，太子詹事崔湜為中書侍郎，並同中書門下三品；

translations.literal: Liu Youqiu, Minister of Personnel, was made Palace Attendant; Wei Zhigu, Right Regular Attendant, was made Left Regular Attendant; Cui Shi, crown prince's chief steward, was made Vice Director of the Secretariat—all with third-rank standing.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Youqiu became Palace Attendant; Wei Zhigu became Left Regular Attendant; Cui Shi became Vice Director of the Secretariat—all raised to third rank.

sentences.zh: 書中侍郎陸象先同平章事。

translations.literal: Lu Xiangxian, Vice Director of the Secretariat, was also made Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xiangxian, Vice Director of the Secretariat, was also made Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 皆太平公主之志也。

translations.literal: All of this accorded with Princess Taiping's wishes.
translations.idiomatic: Every appointment reflected Princess Taiping's design.

sentences.zh: 像先清淨寡慾，言論高遠，為時人所重。

translations.literal: Xiangxian was pure and quiet, with few desires; his discourse was lofty, and the age esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xiangxian lived plainly; his words carried weight, and the age respected him.

sentences.zh: 湜私侍太平公主，公主欲引以為相，湜請與象先同升，公主不可，湜曰：「然則湜亦不敢當。」

translations.literal: Shi privately attended the princess; she wished to make him chancellor. Shi asked to rise with Xiangxian; she refused. Shi said, 'Then I dare not accept.'
translations.idiomatic: Cui Shi was the princess's favorite; she meant to make him chief minister. He asked that Lu Xiangxian rise with him; she refused. 'Then I dare not take the office,' he said.

sentences.zh: 公主乃為之並言於上。

translations.literal: The princess then spoke for both to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: The princess then pleaded for both before the throne.

sentences.zh: 上不欲用湜，公主涕泣以請，乃從之。

translations.literal: The emperor did not wish to use Shi, but the princess wept until he yielded.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was reluctant, but the princess wept until he gave way.

sentences.zh: 右補闕辛替否上疏，以為：「自古失道破國亡家者，口說不如身逢，耳聞不如目睹。

translations.literal: Right Remonstrance Official Xin Tifu submitted a memorial: 'From antiquity, those who lost the Way and ruined states—hearsay is not equal to what the body has met; the ear is not equal to the eye.
translations.idiomatic: Xin Tifu memorialized: 'Rulers who lost the Way learned more from experience than from hearsay, more from their own eyes than from others' tongues.

sentences.zh: 臣請以陛下所目睹者言之。

translations.literal: Your servant asks to speak from what Your Majesty has seen.
translations.idiomatic: I beg to speak from what Your Majesty has witnessed.

sentences.zh: 太宗皇帝，陛下之祖也，撥亂返正，開基立極；

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong, Your Majesty's ancestor, quelled disorder and restored order, founding the dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong, your grandfather, swept away chaos and laid the foundation of the realm.

sentences.zh: 官不虛授，財無枉費；

translations.literal: Offices were not given in vain; wealth was not wasted without cause.
translations.idiomatic: He gave no office without merit and spent no coin without reason.

sentences.zh: 不多造寺觀而有福，不多度僧尼而無災，天地垂祐，風雨時若，粟帛充溢，蠻夷率服，享國久長，名高萬古。

translations.literal: He did not build many temples yet possessed good fortune; he did not ordain many clergy yet suffered no calamity. Heaven favored him; wind and rain came in season; grain overflowed; barbarians submitted; the dynasty endured; its fame towers through the ages.
translations.idiomatic: He built few temples yet prospered, ordained few clergy yet knew no disaster. Heaven smiled, harvests brimmed, the frontier bowed, and Tang endured—its name bright across the ages.

sentences.zh: 陛下何不取而法之！

translations.literal: Why does Your Majesty not take this as his model!
translations.idiomatic: Why not take him as your model?

sentences.zh: 中宗皇帝，陛下之兄，棄祖宗之業，徇女子之意；

translations.literal: Emperor Zhongzong, Your Majesty's brother, abandoned the ancestors' work and indulged women's wishes.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhongzong cast aside the founders' legacy and bent to women's will.

sentences.zh: 無能而祿者數千人，無功而封者百餘家；

translations.literal: Those without ability yet on salary numbered in the thousands; those without merit yet enfeoffed numbered in the hundreds.
translations.idiomatic: Thousands drew stipends without talent; hundreds received fiefs without service.

sentences.zh: 造寺不止，費財貨者數百億，度人無窮，免租庸者數十萬，所出日滋，所入日寡；

translations.literal: Temple building never ceased; spending ran to tens of billions; ordinations were endless; tax exemptions numbered in the hundreds of thousands. Outflow increased daily; inflow dwindled.
translations.idiomatic: Monasteries rose without end at vast cost; ordinations never stopped; hundreds of thousands were freed from tax. Spending mounted while revenue shrank.

sentences.zh: 奪百姓口中之食以養貪殘，剝萬人體上之衣以塗土木，於是人怨神怒，眾叛親離，水旱並臻，公私俱罄，享國不永，禍及其身。

translations.literal: He seized food from the people's mouths to feed the greedy and stripped garments from ten thousand bodies to plaster earth and timber. Men resented; the gods raged; the masses rebelled; flood and drought came; stores were emptied; the reign did not last; calamity reached his person.
translations.idiomatic: He took bread from common mouths to feed the rapacious and stripped the people's clothes to gild brick and timber. Men cursed, heaven raged, subjects turned away; flood and drought struck; the treasury drained; the reign proved brief; ruin overtook him.

sentences.zh: 陛下何不懲而改之！

translations.literal: Why does Your Majesty not take warning and reform!
translations.idiomatic: Why not take that as your warning and turn back?

sentences.zh: 自頃以來，水旱相繼，兼以霜蝗，人無所食，未聞賑恤，而為二女造觀，用錢百餘萬婚。

translations.literal: In recent times flood and drought have followed one another, with frost and locusts; the people have nothing to eat. No relief is heard of, yet abbeys are built for two daughters at a cost of more than a million strings of cash.
translations.idiomatic: Lately flood, drought, frost, and locusts have left people starving while no relief is offered—yet two abbeys are raised for the princesses at a cost of more than a million strings.

sentences.zh: 陛下豈可不計當今府庫之蓄積有幾，中外之經費有幾，而輕用百餘萬緡，以供無用之役乎！

translations.literal: How can Your Majesty fail to reckon the treasury's stores and the realm's expenses, yet lightly spend more than a million strings on a useless undertaking!
translations.idiomatic: Will you not count what the treasury holds and what the realm must spend before throwing a million strings at so useless a project?

sentences.zh: 陛下族韋氏之家，而不去韋氏之惡，忍棄太宗之法，不忍棄中宗之政乎！

translations.literal: Your Majesty exterminated the Wei clan yet did not cast off the Wei's evils. Will you abandon Taizong's laws yet not abandon Zhongzong's policies!
translations.idiomatic: You destroyed the Wei root and branch yet kept their ways. You can forsake Taizong's code—but not Zhongzong's habits?

sentences.zh: 且陛下與太子當韋氏用事之時，日夕憂危，切齒於群凶；

translations.literal: Moreover, when Your Majesty and the crown prince were under the Wei's grip, day and night you lived in fear, gnashing your teeth at that villainous band.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wei faction held sway, you and the heir lived in daily dread, your teeth set against those villains.

sentences.zh: 今幸而除之，乃不改其所為，臣恐復有切齒於陛下者也。

translations.literal: Now, having removed them, you yet do not change what they did. I fear there will again be those who gnash their teeth at Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: You have removed them—yet you repeat their conduct. I fear others will soon grind their teeth at you.

sentences.zh: 然則陛下又何惡於群凶而誅之！

translations.literal: In that case, why did Your Majesty hate that band enough to execute them!
translations.idiomatic: If so, why did you hate those villains enough to kill them?

sentences.zh: 昔先帝之憐悖逆也，宗晉卿為之造第，趙履溫為之葺園，殫園財，竭人力，第成不暇居，園成不暇游，而身為戮沒。

translations.literal: Formerly, when the late emperor indulged the rebel prince, Zong Jinqing built him a mansion and Zhao Luwen laid out gardens, exhausting wealth and labor. Mansion and garden were finished with no time to enjoy them—yet he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: When the late emperor doted on the rebel prince, Zong Jinqing built him a palace and Zhao Luwen planted gardens at ruinous cost. Palace and garden were finished before he could enjoy either—and then he was slain.

sentences.zh: 今之造觀崇侈者，必非陛下、公主之本意，殆有宗、趙之徒從而勸之，不可不察也。

translations.literal: Today's abbey-building cannot be Your Majesty and the princess's true intent; likely men like Zong and Zhao urge it on. This cannot go unexamined.
translations.idiomatic: This lavish building cannot be your true wish. Men like Zong and Zhao are surely whispering again. Look closely.

sentences.zh: 陛下不停斯役，臣恐人之愁怨，不減先朝之時。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty does not halt this labor, I fear the people's resentment will match the previous reign.
translations.idiomatic: If you do not stop this work, the people's bitterness will match the last emperor's day.

sentences.zh: 人人知其禍敗，而口不敢言，言則刑戮隨之。

translations.literal: Everyone knows ruin awaits, yet none dares speak; speech invites execution.
translations.idiomatic: All see disaster coming, yet none dare speak—speech means the block.

sentences.zh: 如韋月將、燕欽融之徒，先朝誅之，陛下賞之，豈非陛下知直言之有益於國乎！

translations.literal: Men such as Wei Yuejiang and Yan Qinrong—the previous reign executed them, yet Your Majesty has rewarded them. Is this not because Your Majesty knows straight speech benefits the state!
translations.idiomatic: Wei Yuejiang and Yan Qinrong spoke plainly; the last reign killed them, yet you have honored them. Surely you know honest counsel serves the realm!

sentences.zh: 臣今所言，亦先朝之直也，惟陛下察之。」

translations.literal: What I speak now is likewise the straight speech of the previous reign. May Your Majesty examine it.'
translations.idiomatic: What I say now is the same plain truth they died for. I beg Your Majesty to weigh it.'

sentences.zh: 上雖不能從，而嘉其切直。

translations.literal: Though the emperor could not follow the advice, he praised its earnest directness.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor could not act on the memorial, but he commended its blunt honesty.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞和逢堯攝鴻臚卿，使於突厥，說默啜曰：「處密、堅昆聞可汗結昏於唐，皆當歸附。

translations.literal: Vice Censor He Fengyao, acting Director of Banquets, was sent to the Turks and said to Mo-chuo: 'When Chumiji and Jiankun hear you have allied by marriage with Tang, they will all submit.
translations.idiomatic: He Fengyao, Vice Censor and acting Director of Banquets, told Mo-chuo: 'Once Chumiji and Jiankun hear you have wed the Tang court, they will come over.

sentences.zh: 可汗何不襲唐冠帶，使諸胡知之，豈不美哉！」

translations.literal: Why does the khan not adopt Tang cap and sash, so all the Hu may know—would that not be splendid!'
translations.idiomatic: Why not take Tang dress and cap and let every tribe see it? Would that not be fine?'

sentences.zh: 默啜許諾，明日，襆頭、衣紫衫，南向再拜，稱臣，遣其子楊我支及國相隨逢堯入朝，十一月，戊寅，至京師。

translations.literal: Mo-chuo agreed. The next day he put on a turban and purple robe, faced south and bowed twice, styled himself subject, and sent his son Yang Wuzhi and the chancellor to follow Fengyao into court. Eleventh month, wuyin, they reached the capital.
