translations.idiomatic: Mo-chuo consented. The next day he donned Tang dress, bowed toward the south, declared himself a vassal, and sent his son Yang Wuzhi and his chancellor to court with Fengyao. Eleventh month, wuyin: they reached the capital.

sentences.zh: 逢堯以奉使功，遷戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: Fengyao, for the merit of his mission, was transferred to Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: For his embassy, He Fengyao was promoted to Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，令天下百姓二十五入軍，五十五免。

translations.literal: On the day renchen, an edict was issued: throughout the realm, commoners at twenty-five were to enter military service, and at fifty-five were to be released.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen, the throne ordered universal conscription at age twenty-five and discharge at fifty-five.

sentences.zh: 十二月，癸卯，以興昔亡可汗阿史那獻為招慰十姓使。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on the day guimao, Ashina Xian, the khan of Xingxi who had fled, was appointed Commissioner to Pacify and Console the Ten Surnames.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on guimao, Ashina Xian—the exiled Khan of Xingxi—was named envoy to win over the Ten Surname tribes.

sentences.zh: 上召天台山道士司馬承禎，問以陰陽數術，對曰：「道者，損之又損，以至於無為，安肯勞心以學術數乎！」

translations.literal: The emperor summoned the Tiantai Mountain Daoist Sima Chengzhen and questioned him concerning yin-yang and the arts of number. He replied: 'The Way is to diminish and diminish again until one reaches nonaction—how could one willingly toil the mind learning arts of calculation!'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned Sima Chengzhen, a Daoist of Mount Tiantai, and asked him about yin-yang lore and divination. Chengzhen answered: 'The Way is ever to lessen and lessen, until one arrives at nonaction. Why would anyone weary the heart studying the tricks of number and fate?'

sentences.zh: 上曰：「理身無為則高矣，如理國何？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: 'Nonaction in ordering the body is lofty indeed—but what of ordering the state?'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: 'To govern oneself through nonaction is sublime—but what of governing the realm?'

sentences.zh: 對曰：「國猶身也，順物自然而心無所私，則天下理矣。」

translations.literal: He replied: 'The state is like the body. Follow things in their natural course and let the heart harbor no private ends, and all under Heaven will be well ordered.'
translations.idiomatic: He answered: 'The realm is like the body. Yield to the natural way of things, keep the heart free of selfish design, and the empire will govern itself.'

sentences.zh: 上歎曰：「廣成之言，無以過也。」

translations.literal: The emperor sighed and said: 'The words of Guangchengzi—nothing surpasses them.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sighed: 'The teaching of Guangchengzi could not be bettered.'

sentences.zh: 承禎固請還山，上許之。

translations.literal: Chengzhen firmly requested to return to the mountains; the emperor granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Chengzhen pressed earnestly to return to his mountain retreat, and the emperor consented.

sentences.zh: 尚書左丞盧藏用指終南山謂承禎曰：「此中大有佳處，何必天台！」

translations.literal: Left Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs Lu Zangyong pointed to Mount Zhongnan and said to Chengzhen: 'There are excellent places here—why must you go to Tiantai!'
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zangyong, Left Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs, gestured toward Mount Zhongnan and told Chengzhen: 'These hills hold every delight—why trouble yourself with Tiantai?'

sentences.zh: 承禎曰：「以愚觀之，此乃仕宦之疾徑耳！」

translations.literal: Chengzhen said: 'In my humble view, this is merely a shortcut for official ambition!'
translations.idiomatic: Chengzhen replied: 'As I see it, this is nothing but the fast track to office and rank!'

sentences.zh: 藏用嘗隱終南，則天時征為左拾遺，故承禎言之。

translations.literal: Zangyong had once lived in reclusion on Zhongnan; in Empress Wu's time he was summoned as Left Reminder—hence Chengzhen's remark.
translations.idiomatic: Zangyong had once retired to Zhongnan, only to be summoned under Empress Wu as Left Reminder of the Palace—hence Chengzhen's barb.

sentences.zh: 玄宗至道大聖大明孝皇帝上之上

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong, the Most Sage Divine Great Bright Filial Emperor—above, Part One.
translations.idiomatic: The Reign of Emperor Xuanzong (First Section)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，辛巳，睿宗祀南郊，初用諫議大夫賈曾議合祭天地。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on the day xinsi, Ruizong sacrificed at the Southern Suburb, for the first time adopting Remonstrance and Counselor Jia Zeng's proposal to joint-sacrifice Heaven and Earth.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on xinsi, Emperor Ruizong offered sacrifice at the Southern Suburb, inaugurating the joint rite of Heaven and Earth as urged by Remonstrance and Counselor Jia Zeng.

sentences.zh: 曾，言忠之子也。

translations.literal: Zeng was the son of Yanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Zeng was the son of Jia Yanzhong.

sentences.zh: 戊子，幸滻東，耕籍田。

translations.literal: On the day wuzi, [the emperor] visited Chan east [of the capital] and plowed the sacred field.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi, the emperor traveled east to Chan and performed the ceremonial plowing of the sacred field.

sentences.zh: 己丑，赦天下；

translations.literal: On the day jichou, [he] pardoned all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou, he proclaimed a general amnesty throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 改元太極。

translations.literal: The era name was changed to Taiji.
translations.idiomatic: The reign era was renamed Taiji.

sentences.zh: 乙未，上御安福門，宴突厥楊我支，以金山公主示之；

translations.literal: On the day yiwei, the emperor attended at Anfu Gate, feasted the Turk Yang Wozhi, and showed him Princess Jinshan.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei, the emperor presided at Anfu Gate, entertained the Turk envoy Yang Wozhi, and presented Princess Jinshan to him.

sentences.zh: 既而會上傳位，婚竟不成。

translations.literal: Then, as it happened, the emperor abdicated, and the marriage in the end did not come to pass.
translations.idiomatic: But the emperor soon abdicated, and the marriage was never concluded.

sentences.zh: 以左御史大夫竇懷貞、戶部尚書岑羲並同中書門下三品。

translations.literal: Left Censor-in-Chief Dou Huaizhen and Minister of Revenue Cen Xi were both appointed co-Chancellors of the Secretariat and Chancellery of the Third Rank.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Huaizhen, Left Censor-in-Chief, and Cen Xi, Minister of Revenue, were both made Grand Councilors of the Third Rank.

sentences.zh: 二月，辛酉，廢右御史台。

translations.literal: In the second month, on the day xinyou, the Right Censorate was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on xinyou, the Right Censorate was dissolved.

sentences.zh: 蒲州刺史蕭至忠自托於太平公主，公主引為刑部尚書。

translations.literal: Prefect of Puzhou Xiao Zhizhong attached himself to Princess Taiping; the princess brought him in as Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Zhizhong, prefect of Puzhou, placed himself under Princess Taiping's patronage, and she had him appointed Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 華州長史蔣欽緒，其妹夫也，謂之曰：「如子之才，何憂不達！

translations.literal: Chief Secretary of Huazhou Jiang Qinxu, his brother-in-law, said to him: 'With talent such as yours, why worry you will not rise!
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Qinxu, chief secretary of Huazhou and Zhizhong's brother-in-law, told him: 'With gifts like yours, what need is there to fear advancement?

sentences.zh: 勿為非分妄求。」

translations.literal: Do not seek what is not yours in reckless ambition.'
translations.idiomatic: Do not grasp after what is not rightfully yours.'

sentences.zh: 至忠不應。

translations.literal: Zhizhong did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Zhizhong made no answer.

sentences.zh: 欽緒退，歎曰：「九代卿族，一舉滅之，可哀也哉！」

translations.literal: Qinxu withdrew and sighed: 'A ministerial clan of nine generations—destroyed in one stroke. How lamentable!'
translations.idiomatic: As Qinxu withdrew, he sighed: 'Nine generations of ministerial rank—undone in a single reckless move. What a pity!'

sentences.zh: 至忠素有雅望，嘗自公主第門出，遇宋璟，璟曰：「非所望於蕭君也。」

translations.literal: Zhizhong had long enjoyed an upright reputation; once, exiting the princess's mansion gate, he encountered Song Jing, who said: 'This is not what was expected of Master Xiao.'
translations.idiomatic: Zhizhong had long borne a name for integrity. Once, as he came out of the princess's gate, he met Song Jing, who said: 'This is not what one hoped to see from you, Master Xiao.'

sentences.zh: 至忠笑曰：「善乎宋生之言！」

translations.literal: Zhizhong smiled and said: 'How well said, young Song!'
translations.idiomatic: Zhizhong smiled: 'Well put, young Song!'

sentences.zh: 遽策馬而去。

translations.literal: He immediately spurred his horse and left.
translations.idiomatic: He wheeled his horse at once and rode away.

sentences.zh: 幽州大都督薛訥鎮幽州二十餘年，吏民安之。

translations.literal: Great Protector-General of Youzhou Xue Ne garrisoned Youzhou for more than twenty years; officials and people found peace under him.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Ne, Great Protector-General of Youzhou, had held the frontier for more than twenty years, and officials and commoners alike lived in security under his rule.

sentences.zh: 未嘗舉兵出塞，虜亦不敢犯。

translations.literal: He never once raised troops beyond the passes; the barbarians likewise dared not invade.
translations.idiomatic: He never led an army beyond the border forts, and the nomads in turn did not dare cross in.

sentences.zh: 與燕州刺史李璡有隙，璡毀之於劉幽求，幽求薦左羽林將軍孫佺代之。

translations.literal: He had a rift with Prefect of Yanzhou Li Jin; Jin slandered him to Liu Youqiu, who recommended Left General-of-the-Feathered Forest Sun Wan to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: He fell out with Li Jin, prefect of Yanzhou. Jin denounced him to Liu Youqiu, who recommended Left General of the Feathered Forest Sun Wan to take his place.

sentences.zh: 三月，丁丑，以佺為幽州大都督，徙訥為并州長史。

translations.literal: In the third month, on the day dingchou, Wan was made Great Protector-General of Youzhou and Ne was transferred to be chief secretary of Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on dingchou, Sun Wan was appointed Great Protector-General of Youzhou, and Xue Ne was reassigned as chief secretary of Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 夏，五月，益州獠反。

translations.literal: In summer, the fifth month, the Liao of Yizhou rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fifth month, the Liao tribes of Yizhou rose in revolt.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，上祭北郊。

translations.literal: On the day wuyin, the emperor sacrificed at the Northern Suburb.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin, the emperor offered sacrifice at the Northern Suburb.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，赦天下，改元延和。

translations.literal: On the day xinsi, [he] pardoned all under Heaven and changed the era name to Yanhe.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi, he proclaimed a general amnesty and renamed the era Yanhe.

sentences.zh: 六月，丁未，右散騎常侍武攸暨卒，追封定王，

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on the day dingwei, Right Attendant Cavalier-at-Court Wu Youji died and was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Ding.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on dingwei, Right Attendant Cavalier-at-Court Wu Youji died and was posthumously created Prince of Ding.

sentences.zh: 上以節愍太子之亂，岑羲有保護之功，癸丑，以羲為侍中。

translations.literal: Because during the upheaval of Crown Prince Jiemin, Cen Xi had merit in protecting [the emperor], on the day guichou [the emperor] made Xi Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In recognition of Cen Xi's service in shielding the throne during the turmoil of Crown Prince Jiemin, on guichou the emperor appointed him Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 庚申，幽州大都督孫佺與奚酋李大酺戰於冷陘，全軍覆沒。

translations.literal: On the day gengshen, Great Protector-General of Youzhou Sun Wan fought the Xi chieftain Li Dapu at Lengyu Pass; the entire army was destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen, Sun Wan, Great Protector-General of Youzhou, clashed with the Xi chieftain Li Dapu at Cold Gorge Pass—and his whole force was annihilated.

sentences.zh: 是時，佺帥左驍衛將軍李楷洛，左威衛將軍周以悌發兵二萬、騎八千，分為三軍，以襲奚、契丹。

translations.literal: At this time, Wan led Left General-of-the-Vigorous Guard Li Kailuo and Left General-of-the-Awe-Inspiring Guard Zhou Yiti, mobilizing twenty thousand infantry and eight thousand cavalry, divided into three armies, to strike the Xi and Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: By then Sun Wan had marched under Left General of the Vigorous Guard Li Kailuo and Left General of the Awe-Inspiring Guard Zhou Yiti with twenty thousand foot soldiers and eight thousand horsemen, split into three columns, to strike the Xi and Khitan.

sentences.zh: 將軍烏可利諫曰：「道險而天熱，懸軍遠襲，往必敗。」

translations.literal: General Wu Keli remonstrated: 'The route is perilous and the weather hot—sending troops far on a distant raid, you will surely be defeated.'
translations.idiomatic: General Wu Keli warned him: 'The road is treacherous and the heat fierce. To drive an army deep into enemy country on such a raid is to invite disaster.'

sentences.zh: 佺曰：薛訥在邊積年，竟不能為國家復營州。

translations.literal: Wan said: 'Xue Ne spent years on the frontier yet in the end could not recover Yingzhou for the state.'
translations.idiomatic: Sun Wan replied: 'Xue Ne held the border for years and still could not win back Yingzhou for the empire.'

sentences.zh: 今乘其無備，往必有功。

translations.literal: Now we strike while they are unprepared—we will surely succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Now we catch them off guard—victory is certain.

sentences.zh: 使楷洛將騎四千前驅，遇奚騎八千，楷洛戰不利。

translations.literal: He sent Kailuo with four thousand cavalry as vanguard; they encountered eight thousand Xi horsemen and Kailuo fared poorly in battle.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Li Kailuo ahead with four thousand cavalry. They met eight thousand Xi riders, and Kailuo was driven back.

sentences.zh: 佺怯懦，不敢救，引軍欲還，虜乘之，唐兵大敗。

translations.literal: Wan was timid and dared not rescue; he drew off his army intending to retreat, the enemy pressed the advantage, and Tang troops suffered great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Wan, too cowardly to reinforce him, began to withdraw—and the enemy pressed hard, routing the Tang army.

sentences.zh: 佺阻山為方陳以自固，大酺使謂佺曰：「朝廷既與我和親，今大軍何為而來？」

translations.literal: Wan barred the mountains in a square formation to fortify himself; Dapu sent word to Wan: 'The court already made peace-marriage with us—why has your great army come now?'
translations.idiomatic: Sun Wan drew up a square formation against the hills to hold his ground. Li Dapu sent a messenger: 'Your court has already bound us in marriage alliance—why does a great army come now?'

sentences.zh: 佺曰：「吾奉敕來招慰耳。

translations.literal: Wan said: 'I come only under imperial order to pacify and console.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Wan answered: 'I come only under imperial command to offer reassurance and goodwill.

sentences.zh: 楷洛不稟節度，輒與汝戰，請斬以謝。」

translations.literal: Kailuo disobeyed command and rashly fought you—please allow me to execute him to apologize.'
translations.idiomatic: Li Kailuo defied my orders and attacked you of his own accord. Permit me to behead him in atonement.'

sentences.zh: 大酺曰：「若然，國信安在？」

translations.literal: Dapu said: 'If so, where stands the trust of the state?'
translations.idiomatic: Li Dapu said: 'If that is so, what becomes of the good faith of your empire?'

sentences.zh: 佺悉斂軍中帛，得萬餘段，並紫袍、金帶、魚袋以贈之。

translations.literal: Wan gathered all silk in the army, obtaining more than ten thousand bolts, together with purple robes, gold belts, and fish purses, and presented them as gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Wan collected every bolt of silk in the camp—more than ten thousand in all—along with purple robes, gold belts, and official fish purses, and sent them as gifts.

sentences.zh: 大酺曰：「請將軍南還，勿相驚擾。」

translations.literal: Dapu said: 'Please, General, return south—let us not alarm and harass each other.'
translations.idiomatic: Li Dapu said: 'General, withdraw to the south, and let neither side trouble the other further.'

sentences.zh: 將士懼，無復部伍，虜追擊之，士卒皆潰。

translations.literal: The officers and soldiers were afraid; ranks were no longer kept; the barbarians pursued and struck them, and the troops all broke and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Officers and soldiers panicked and lost all formation. The enemy chased them down, and the whole force scattered in rout.

sentences.zh: 佺、以悌為虜所擒，獻於突厥，默啜皆殺之；

translations.literal: Wan and Yiti were captured by the barbarians, presented to the Turks, and Mo-chu executed them both;
translations.idiomatic: Sun Wan and Zhou Yiti were taken captive, handed over to the Turks, and Khaghan Moqur put them both to death;

sentences.zh: 楷洛、可利脫歸。

translations.literal: Kailuo and Keli escaped and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Li Kailuo and Wu Keli broke free and made it back.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，彗星出西方，經軒轅入太微，至於大角。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, a comet appeared in the west, passed through Xuanyuan, entered the Supreme Palace Enclosure, and reached the Horn.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, a comet rose in the west, swept through Xuanyuan into the Supreme Palace Enclosure, and reached the Horn star.

sentences.zh: 有相者謂同中書門下三品竇懷貞曰：「公有刑厄。」

translations.literal: A physiognomist said to Grand Counselor of the Third Rank Dou Huai'zhen: "Your lordship faces punishment and calamity."
translations.idiomatic: A fortune-teller told Dou Huai'zhen, co-chancellor of the third rank: "You face a sentence of punishment."

sentences.zh: 懷貞懼，請解官為安國寺奴；

translations.literal: Huai'zhen was afraid and requested to resign office and become a slave of Anguo Temple;
translations.idiomatic: Dou Huai'zhen was terrified and asked to resign and serve as a temple slave at Anguo Abbey;

sentences.zh: 敕聽解官。

translations.literal: An edict permitted him to resign.
translations.idiomatic: The throne granted his resignation.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，復以懷貞為左僕射兼御史大夫、平章軍國重事。

translations.literal: On the day yihai, Huai'zhen was again made Left Vice Director, concurrently Censor-in-Chief, and co-manager of weighty affairs of state and army.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai, Dou Huai'zhen was restored as Left Vice Director, Censor-in-Chief, and co-chancellor for state and military affairs.

sentences.zh: 太平公主使術者言於上曰：「彗所以除舊布新，又帝座及心前星皆有變，皇太子當為天子。」

translations.literal: Princess Taiping had a diviner speak to the emperor, saying: "A comet is meant to remove the old and spread the new; moreover the Imperial Seat and the star before the Heart have both changed—the crown prince ought to become Son of Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: Princess Taiping had a soothsayer tell the emperor: "Comets sweep away the old to make way for the new—and both the Imperial Seat and the star before the Heart have shifted. The crown prince is destined for the throne."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「傳德避災，吾志決矣！」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "To transmit virtue and avert calamity—my mind is made up!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "I will pass on my virtue to avert disaster—my decision is firm!"

sentences.zh: 太平公主及其黨皆力諫，以為不可。

translations.literal: Princess Taiping and her faction all remonstrated forcefully, holding that it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Taiping and her allies all pressed him hard, insisting it must not be done.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「中宗之時，群奸用事，天變屢臻。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "In Zhongzong's time, a pack of villains held power, and heavenly portents came again and again.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Under Zhongzong, villains ran the court and omens piled up one after another.

sentences.zh: 朕時請中宗擇賢子立之以應災異，中宗不悅，朕憂恐，數日不食。

translations.literal: At that time I asked Zhongzong to choose a worthy son and install him to answer the heavenly anomaly; Zhongzong was displeased; I was anxious and afraid, and for several days ate nothing.
translations.idiomatic: I then urged Zhongzong to name a worthy son and set him up to answer the omen. He took it ill. I was sick with fear and would not eat for days.

sentences.zh: 豈可在彼則能勸之，在己則不能邪！」

translations.literal: How can I have urged it then and yet be unable to do it now!
translations.idiomatic: How can I have counselled that then and refuse to act on it now!"

sentences.zh: 太子聞之，馳入見，自投於地，叩頭請曰：「臣以微功，不次為嗣，懼不克堪，未審陛下遽以大位傳之，何也？」

translations.literal: When the crown prince heard this, he galloped in to audience, threw himself to the ground, and kowtowed, saying: "Your servant, by slight merit, was raised out of turn to be heir; I fear I cannot bear the burden. I do not understand why Your Majesty would suddenly pass the great throne—why?"
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince heard this, he rushed in, flung himself to the floor, and kowtowed: "I was made heir ahead of my deserts by a small service, and I fear I am not equal to the charge. Why would Your Majesty suddenly hand me the throne?"

sentences.zh: 上曰：「社稷所以再安，吾之所以得天下，皆汝力也。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The altars of soil and grain were twice restored to peace, and the reason I obtained all under Heaven—all is your doing.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "The realm was twice brought back to peace, and I owe the throne to you alone.

sentences.zh: 今帝座有災，故以授汝，轉禍為福，汝何疑邪！」

translations.literal: Now the Imperial Seat has calamity; therefore I give it to you—turn misfortune into fortune. Why do you doubt!
translations.idiomatic: Now the Imperial Seat is under a sign of disaster, so I give it to you—turning ill luck to good. What is there to doubt!"

sentences.zh: 太子固辭。

translations.literal: The crown prince firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince refused again and again.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「汝為孝子，何必待柩前然後即位邪！」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "You are a filial son—why must you wait until before the coffin to ascend the throne!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "A filial son need not wait for the bier to take the throne!"

sentences.zh: 太子流涕而出。

translations.literal: The crown prince wept as he withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince withdrew in tears.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，制傳位於太子，太子上表固辭。

translations.literal: On the day renchen, an edict transmitted the throne to the crown prince; the crown prince submitted a memorial firmly declining.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen, an edict passed the throne to the crown prince; he memorialized a firm refusal.

sentences.zh: 太平公主勸上雖傳位，猶宜自總大政。

translations.literal: Princess Taiping urged the emperor that though he should transmit the throne, he still ought personally to hold overall governance.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Taiping urged that even after abdicating he should still keep the reins of power.

sentences.zh: 上乃謂太子曰：「汝以天下事重，欲朕兼理之邪？」

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon said to the crown prince: "You hold the affairs of all under Heaven weighty—do you wish me to govern jointly?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then asked the crown prince: "You find the burden of empire heavy—do you want me to share the rule?"

sentences.zh: 昔舜禪禹，猶親巡狩。

translations.literal: In antiquity, when Shun ceded to Yu, he still personally went on inspection tours.
translations.idiomatic: When Shun yielded to Yu, he still went on tour in person.

sentences.zh: 聯雖傳位，豈忘家國？

translations.literal: Though I cede the throne, how could I forget family and state?
translations.idiomatic: Though I yield the throne, shall I forget home and realm?

sentences.zh: 其軍國大事，當兼省之。

translations.literal: As for great affairs of state and army, I shall jointly oversee them.
translations.idiomatic: On military and state affairs of first importance, I shall still share oversight.

sentences.zh: 八月，庚子，玄宗即位，尊睿宗為太上皇。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on the day gengzi, Xuanzong ascended the throne and honored Ruizong as Retired Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on gengzi, Xuanzong took the throne and ennobled Ruizong as Retired Emperor.

sentences.zh: 上皇自稱曰朕，命曰誥，五日一受朝於太極殿。

translations.literal: The Retired Emperor styled himself zhen, his orders gao, and every five days received court once at Taiji Hall.
translations.idiomatic: The Retired Emperor called himself zhen, issued gao, and held court at Taiji Hall once every five days.

sentences.zh: 皇帝自稱曰予，命曰制、敕，日受朝於武德殿。

translations.literal: The emperor styled himself yu, his orders zhi and chi, and daily received court at Wude Hall.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor called himself yu, issued zhi and chi, and held daily court at Wude Hall.

sentences.zh: 三品以上除授及大刑政決於上皇，餘皆決於皇帝。

translations.literal: Appointments and removals of third rank and above, and great punishments and government, were decided by the Retired Emperor; all else was decided by the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Third-rank appointments and capital crimes fell to the Retired Emperor; everything else to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，上大聖天後尊號曰聖帝天後。

translations.literal: On the day renyin, the emperor gave the Great Sage Empress Dowager the honorific title Sage-Emperor Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin, the Great Sage Empress Dowager was styled Sage-Emperor Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，赦天下，改元。

translations.literal: On the day jiachen, all under Heaven was amnestied and the era name was changed.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen, the realm was amnestied and the reign era renamed.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，於漠州北置渤海軍，恆、定州境置恆陽軍，媯、蔚州境置懷柔軍，屯兵五萬。

translations.literal: On the day yisi, at north of Mochou Prefecture Bohai Army was established; in the territory of Heng and Ding prefectures Hengyang Army was established; in the territory of Gui and Yu prefectures Huairou Army was established—fifty thousand troops were garrisoned.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi, Bohai Army was posted north of Mochou; Hengyang Army on the Heng and Ding frontier; Huairou Army on the Gui and Yu frontier—fifty thousand men in all.

sentences.zh: 丙午，立妃王氏為皇后，以後父仁皎為太僕卿。

translations.literal: On the day bingwu, Consort Wang was installed as empress, and the empress's father Renjiao was made Grand Master of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu, Lady Wang was made empress and her father Wang Renjiao appointed Grand Master of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 仁皎，下邽人也。

translations.literal: Renjiao was a native of Xiaji.
translations.idiomatic: Renjiao came from Xiaji.

sentences.zh: 戊申，立皇子許昌王嗣直為郯王，真定王嗣謙為郢王。

translations.literal: On the day wushen, the emperor's son Prince of Xuchang Sizhi was made Prince of Tan, and Prince of Zhending Siqian Prince of Ying.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen, Prince Sizhi of Xuchang was created Prince of Tan, and Prince Siqian of Zhending Prince of Ying.

sentences.zh: 以劉幽求為右僕射、同中書門下三品，魏知古為侍中，崔湜為檢校中書令。

translations.literal: Liu Youqiu was made Right Vice Director and co-chancellor of the third rank; Wei Zhigu Attendant-in-Chief; Cui Shi acting Grand Counselor.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Youqiu became Right Vice Director and third-rank co-chancellor; Wei Zhigu, Attendant-in-Chief; Cui Shi, acting Grand Counselor.

sentences.zh: 初，河內王琚預於王同皎之謀，亡命，傭書於江都。

translations.literal: Earlier, Wang Ju of Henei had taken part in Wang Tongjiao's plot, fled as a fugitive, and hired himself out copying books at Jiangdu.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Wang Ju of Henei had joined Wang Tongjiao's conspiracy, gone into hiding, and copied books for hire at Jiangdu.

sentences.zh: 上之為太子也，琚還長安，選補諸暨主簿，過謝太子。

translations.literal: When the emperor was crown prince, Ju returned to Chang'an, was selected and appointed chief clerk of Zhuji, and passed by to thank the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: When the heir was still crown prince, Ju returned to Chang'an, was appointed chief clerk of Zhuji, and came to pay his respects.

sentences.zh: 琚至廷中，故徐行高視，宦者曰：「殿下在簾內。」

translations.literal: Ju reached the courtyard and deliberately walked slowly, looking high; a eunuch said: "His Highness is behind the curtain."
translations.idiomatic: Ju entered the court, strolled in slowly with his chin up; a eunuch said, "His Highness is behind the curtain."

sentences.zh: 琚曰：「何謂殿下？

translations.literal: Ju said: "What do you mean, 'His Highness'?
translations.idiomatic: Ju said, "What 'Highness'?

sentences.zh: 當今獨有太平公主耳！」

translations.literal: Today there is only Princess Taiping!
translations.idiomatic: In this age there is only Princess Taiping!"

sentences.zh: 太子遽召見，與語，琚曰：「韋庶人弒逆，人心不服，誅之易耳。

translations.literal: The crown prince immediately summoned him for audience and spoke with him; Ju said: "Empress Wei committed regicide; men's hearts did not submit—executing her was easy.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince summoned him at once. Ju said: "Empress Wei murdered her sovereign and the people would not follow her—cutting her down was easy.

sentences.zh: 太平公主，武後之子，凶猾無比，大臣多為之用，琚竊憂之。」

translations.literal: Princess Taiping, a child of Empress Wu, is incomparably fierce and cunning; many great ministers serve her—I, Ju, privately worry.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Taiping, Empress Wu's daughter, is savagely cunning, and great ministers do her bidding—I worry for you."

sentences.zh: 太子引與同榻坐，泣曰：「主上同氣，唯有太平，言之恐傷主上之意，不言為患日深，為之奈何？」

translations.literal: The crown prince drew him to sit on the same couch and wept, saying: "Of those of one breath with the sovereign, there is only Taiping; to speak of it would wound the sovereign's feelings, yet not to speak means the trouble grows daily—what is to be done?"
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince pulled him onto the same couch and wept: "The emperor's only close kin is Taiping. To speak may hurt him; to stay silent lets the danger grow—what can I do?"

sentences.zh: 琚曰：「天子之孝，異於匹夫，當以安宗廟社稷為事。

translations.literal: Ju said: "The filial piety of the Son of Heaven differs from that of common men—one should take securing the ancestral temples and altars of soil and grain as one's task.
translations.idiomatic: Ju said: "A Son of Heaven's filial duty is not a common man's—he must secure the ancestral temples and the realm.

sentences.zh: 蓋主，漢昭帝之姊，自幼供養，有罪猶誅之。

translations.literal: Princess Gai, elder sister of Emperor Zhao of Han, was reared from childhood; though she had guilt, she was still executed.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Gai, Emperor Zhao's elder sister, was raised from childhood—yet when she was guilty she was still put to death.

sentences.zh: 為天下者，豈顧小節！」

translations.literal: One who holds all under Heaven—how could he regard small proprieties!
translations.idiomatic: One who holds the empire cannot cling to small points of decorum!"

sentences.zh: 太子悅曰：「君有何藝，可與寡人游？」

translations.literal: The crown prince was pleased and said: "What arts do you have, that you could keep company with me?"
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince was pleased and asked: "What talents have you, that we might keep company?"

sentences.zh: 琚曰：「能飛煉、詼嘲。」

translations.literal: Ju said: "I can refine elixirs and jest."
translations.idiomatic: Ju said: "I can compound elixirs and crack jokes."

sentences.zh: 太子乃奏為詹事府司直，日與游處，累遷太子中舍人；

translations.literal: The crown prince thereupon memorialized to appoint him Rectifier of the Heir Apparent's Household, daily keeping company with him; he was promoted by stages to Attendant of the Heir Apparent;
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince had him appointed rectifier in the heir's household and kept him close day after day, promoting him step by step to attendant of the heir;

sentences.zh: 及即位，以為中書侍郎。

translations.literal: When the emperor ascended the throne, he was made Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanzong took the throne, he was made Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 是時，宰相多太平公主之黨，劉幽求與右羽林將軍張□謀以羽林兵誅之，使□密言於上曰：「竇懷貞、崔湜、岑羲皆因公主得進，日夜為謀不軌。

translations.literal: At this time most chancellors were partisans of Princess Taiping; Liu Youqiu and Right General of the Feathered Forest Zhang Wei plotted to execute them with Feathered Forest troops, and had Wei secretly tell the emperor: "Dou Huai'zhen, Cui Shi, and Cen Xi all advanced through the princess and day and night plot treason.
translations.idiomatic: Most chancellors then were Princess Taiping's men. Liu Youqiu and Zhang Wei, Right General of the Feathered Forest, plotted to kill them with the guard and sent Zhang Wei secretly to tell the emperor: "Dou Huai'zhen, Cui Shi, and Cen Xi all owe their rise to the princess and plot rebellion day and night.

sentences.zh: 若不早圖，一旦事起，太上皇何以得安！

translations.literal: If we do not move early, once the affair breaks out, how can the Retired Emperor be secure!
translations.idiomatic: If we wait, when trouble erupts the Retired Emperor will not be safe!

sentences.zh: 請速誅之。

translations.literal: Please execute them quickly.
translations.idiomatic: Please put them to death at once.

sentences.zh: 臣已與幽求定計，惟俟陛下之命。」

translations.literal: Your servant has already settled the plan with Youqiu; we only await Your Majesty's command.
translations.idiomatic: I have already settled the plan with Youqiu—we await only Your Majesty's order."

sentences.zh: 上深以為然。

translations.literal: The emperor deeply approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor strongly agreed.

sentences.zh: □洩其謀於侍御史鄧光賓，上大懼，遽列上其狀。

translations.literal: Wei leaked the plot to Palace Censor Deng Guangbin; the emperor was greatly afraid and hurriedly submitted the whole account.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wei leaked the plot to Palace Censor Deng Guangbin. The emperor was terrified and immediately reported everything.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，幽求下獄。

translations.literal: On the day bingchen, Youqiu was imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen, Liu Youqiu was thrown into prison.

sentences.zh: 有司奏：「幽求等離間骨肉，罪當死。」

translations.literal: The responsible officials memorialized: "Youqiu and the others drove a wedge between flesh and blood; the crime warrants death."
translations.idiomatic: The prosecutors reported: "Youqiu and the others estranged kin—death is the penalty."

sentences.zh: 上為言幽求有大功，不可殺。

translations.literal: The emperor spoke on Youqiu's behalf, saying he had great merit and could not be killed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor pleaded that Youqiu had great service and must not be executed.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，流幽求於封州，張□於峰州，光賓於繡州。

translations.literal: On the day guihai, Youqiu was exiled to Fengzhou, Zhang Wei to Peak Prefecture, and Guangbin to Xiuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On the day guihai, Youqiu was exiled to Fengzhou, Zhang Wei to Peak Prefecture, and Guangbin to Xiuzhou.

sentences.zh: 初，崔湜為襄州刺史，密與譙王重福通書，重福遺之金帶。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Cui Shi was prefect of Xiangzhou, he secretly exchanged letters with Prince of Qiao Chongfu; Chongfu sent him a gold belt.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, as prefect of Xiangzhou, Cui Shi had secretly corresponded with Prince Chongfu of Qiao, who sent him a gold belt.

sentences.zh: 重福敗，湜當死，張說、劉幽求營護得免。

translations.literal: When Chongfu was defeated, Shi should have died; Zhang Yue and Liu Youqiu interceded and he was spared.
translations.idiomatic: When Chongfu fell, Cui Shi should have died; Zhang Yue and Liu Youqiu saved him.

sentences.zh: 既而湜附太平公主，與公主謀罷說政事，以左丞分司東都。

translations.literal: Thereafter Shi attached himself to Princess Taiping; with the princess he plotted to remove Yue from governing affairs and made him Left Assistant Director serving at the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Then Cui Shi joined Princess Taiping; together they pushed Zhang Yue out of office and sent him to the Eastern Capital as Left Assistant Director without duties.

sentences.zh: 及幽求流封州，湜諷廣州都督周利貞，使殺之。

translations.literal: When Youqiu was exiled to Fengzhou, Shi prompted Prefect of Guangzhou Zhou Lizhen to have him killed.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Youqiu was banished to Fengzhou, Cui Shi urged Zhou Lizhen, prefect of Guangzhou, to kill him.

sentences.zh: 桂州都督景城王晙知其謀，留幽求不遣。

translations.literal: Prefect of Guizhou Wang Jun of Jingcheng knew the plot and detained Youqiu without sending him on.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun of Jingcheng, prefect of Guizhou, learned of the plot and kept Youqiu from being forwarded.

sentences.zh: 利貞屢移牒索之，晙不應，利貞以聞。

translations.literal: Lizhen repeatedly sent documents demanding him; Jun did not respond, and Lizhen reported it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Lizhen repeatedly demanded him by official letter; Wang Jun refused, and Lizhen reported it.

sentences.zh: 湜屢逼晙，使遣幽求，幽求謂晙曰：「公拒執政而保流人，勢不能全，徒仰累耳。」

translations.literal: Shi repeatedly pressed Jun to send Youqiu on; Youqiu said to Jun: "Your lordship resists the chief ministers to protect an exile—by force you cannot save me, and will only bring trouble on yourself."
translations.idiomatic: Cui Shi pressed Wang Jun again and again. Youqiu told Jun: "You defy the chief ministers to shield an exile—you cannot save me and will only harm yourself."

sentences.zh: 固請詣廣州，晙曰：「公所坐非可絕於朋友者也。

translations.literal: He firmly requested to go on to Guangzhou; Jun said: "The offense for which your lordship sits is not one for which one may break with friends.
translations.idiomatic: He insisted on going to Guangzhou. Jun said: "Your offense is not one that should sever friendship.

sentences.zh: 晙因公獲罪，無所恨！」

translations.literal: Jun will be punished because of your lordship—without regret!
translations.idiomatic: If I am punished for you, I shall not regret it!"

sentences.zh: 竟逗遛不遣。

translations.literal: In the end he delayed and did not send him on.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he stalled and would not hand him over.

sentences.zh: 幽求由是得免。

translations.literal: Youqiu thereby escaped death.
translations.idiomatic: Youqiu was thus spared.

sentences.zh: 九月，丁卯朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on dingmao the first day of the month, the sun was eclipsed.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on the dingmao new moon, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，立皇子嗣升為陝王。

translations.literal: On the day xinmao, the emperor's son Prince Sisheng was made Prince of Shan.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao, Prince Sisheng was created Prince of Shan.

sentences.zh: 嗣升母楊氏，士達之曾孫也。

translations.literal: Sisheng's mother Lady Yang was a great-granddaughter of Shida.
translations.idiomatic: Sisheng's mother, Lady Yang, was a great-granddaughter of Yang Shida.

sentences.zh: 王后無子，母養之。

translations.literal: The empress had no son; the mother reared him.
translations.idiomatic: The empress was childless; Lady Yang raised the boy.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，庚子，上謁太廟，赦天下。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on the day gengzi, the emperor visited the Imperial Ancestral Temple and amnestied all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on gengzi, the emperor worshipped at the Imperial Ancestral Temple and proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，上幸新豐，獵於驪山之下。

translations.literal: On the day guimao, the emperor visited Xinfeng and hunted below Mount Li.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao, the emperor went to Xinfeng and hunted at the foot of Mount Li.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，沙陀金山遣使入貢。

translations.literal: On the day xinyou, Jinshan of the Shatuo sent envoys to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou, Jinshan of the Shatuo sent envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 沙陀者，處月之別種也，姓朱邪氏。

translations.literal: The Shatuo are a separate branch of the Chuyue; their surname is Zhuye.
translations.idiomatic: The Shatuo were a branch of the Chuyue, surnamed Zhuye.

sentences.zh: 十一月，乙酉，奚、契丹二萬騎寇漁陽，幽州都督宋璟閉城不出，虜大掠而去。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on the day yiyou, twenty thousand Xi and Khitan horsemen raided Yuyang; Prefect of Youzhou Song Jing closed the city and did not come out; the barbarians plundered heavily and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on yiyou, twenty thousand Xi and Khitan riders struck Yuyang. Song Jing, prefect of Youzhou, shut the gates and would not sally; the raiders looted heavily and left.

sentences.zh: 上皇誥遣皇帝巡邊，西自河、隴，東及燕、薊，選將練卒。

translations.literal: The Retired Emperor issued a gao dispatching the emperor to tour the frontier; from the west from He and Long, east to Yan and Ji, selecting generals and drilling troops.
translations.idiomatic: The Retired Emperor ordered the emperor to tour the frontier—from He and Long in the west to Yan and Ji in the east—to choose commanders and drill soldiers.

sentences.zh: 甲午，以幽州都督宋璟為左軍大總管，并州長史薛訥為中軍大總管，朔方大總管，兵部尚書郭元振為右軍大總管。

translations.literal: On the day jiawu, Prefect of Youzhou Song Jing was made Grand Commander of the Left Army; Chief Secretary of Bingzhou Xue Ne Grand Commander of the Central Army and Grand Protector of Shuofang; Minister of War Guo Yuanzhen Grand Commander of the Right Army.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu, Song Jing, prefect of Youzhou, became Grand Commander of the Left Army; Xue Ne, chief secretary of Bingzhou, Grand Commander of the Central Army and Grand Protector of Shuofang; Guo Yuanzhen, Minister of War, Grand Commander of the Right Army.

sentences.zh: 十二月，刑部尚書李日知請致仕。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Minister of Justice Li Rizhi requested retirement.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, Li Rizhi, Minister of Justice, asked to retire.

sentences.zh: 日知在官，不行捶撻而事集。

translations.literal: While Rizhi held office, he did not apply the beating staff yet affairs were completed.
translations.idiomatic: Li Rizhi governed without ever using the beating rod, yet business was always done.

sentences.zh: 刑部有令史，受敕三日，忘不行。

translations.literal: In the Ministry of Justice there was a clerk who, three days after receiving an edict, forgot and did not act.
translations.idiomatic: A clerk in the Ministry of Justice received an edict and forgot to act on it for three days.

sentences.zh: 日知怒，索杖，集群吏，欲捶之；

translations.literal: Rizhi was angry, demanded the staff, assembled all the clerks, and intended to beat him;
translations.idiomatic: Li Rizhi was furious, called for the rod, gathered the clerks, and was about to flog him;

sentences.zh: 既而謂曰：「我欲捶汝，天下人必謂汝能撩李日知嗔，受李日知杖，不得比於人，妻子亦將棄汝矣。」

translations.literal: Then he said to them: "If I beat you, all under Heaven will say you know how to provoke Li Rizhi's anger and take Li Rizhi's rod—you will not be counted among men, and your wives and children will abandon you too."
translations.idiomatic: Then he told them: "If I beat you, the world will say you knew how to bait Li Rizhi and take his rod—you will be disgraced, and even your families will turn from you."

sentences.zh: 遂釋之。

translations.literal: He thereupon released him.
translations.idiomatic: He let him go.

sentences.zh: 吏皆感悅，無敢犯者，脫有稽失，眾共謫之。

translations.literal: The clerks were all moved and pleased; none dared offend; if there was delay or error, the group together censured him.
translations.idiomatic: The clerks were grateful and dared not err; if anyone slipped, the rest censured him together.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，乙亥，誥：「衛士自今二十五入軍，五十免；

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on the day yihai, a gao: "From now on guardsmen enter service at twenty-five and are released at fifty;
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on yihai, a gao: "Henceforth guardsmen enter service at twenty-five and are discharged at fifty;

sentences.zh: 羽林飛騎並以衛士簡補。」

translations.literal: the Feathered Forest and Flying Cavalry are all to be filled by selection from guardsmen."
translations.idiomatic: Feathered Forest and Flying Cavalry units are to be recruited from the guards."

sentences.zh: 以吏部尚書蕭至忠為中書令。

translations.literal: Minister of the Civil Service Xiao Zhibo was made Grand Counselor.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Zhibo, Minister of the Civil Service, was made Grand Counselor.

sentences.zh: 皇帝巡邊改期，所募兵各散遣，約八月復集，竟不成行。

translations.literal: The emperor's frontier tour was postponed; the troops recruited were each dispersed and sent home, with agreement to assemble again in the eighth month—in the end the tour did not take place.
translations.idiomatic: The frontier tour was postponed; the levies were sent home with orders to reassemble in the eighth month—the expedition never happened.

sentences.zh: 二月，庚子夜，開門然燈，又追作去年大酺，大合伎樂。

translations.literal: In the second month, on the night of gengzi, the gates were opened and lamps lit; they also revived last year's great communal feast, assembling music and performers on a grand scale.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on the night of gengzi, the city gates were opened and lanterns lit; they staged again last year's great puhui, with music and performers on a lavish scale.

sentences.zh: 上皇與上御門樓臨觀，或以夜繼晝，凡月餘。

translations.literal: The Retired Emperor and the emperor mounted the gate tower to watch; sometimes night followed day—for more than a month in all.
translations.idiomatic: Retired Emperor and emperor watched from the gate tower, sometimes feasting from night into day—for more than a month altogether.

sentences.zh: 左拾遺華陰嚴挺之上疏諫，以為：「酺者因人所利，合醵為歡。

translations.literal: Left Reminder Yan Tingzhi of Huayin submitted a memorial remonstrating, holding: "A puhui is something men join for mutual benefit, pooling contributions for merriment.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Tingzhi of Huayin, Left Reminder, memorialized in protest: "A puhui lets people combine what they can spare for shared joy.

sentences.zh: 今乃損萬人之力，營百戲之資，非所以光聖德美風化也。」

translations.literal: Now you are expending the strength of ten thousand men to supply resources for a hundred entertainments—this is not the way to glorify sagely virtue and refine custom.
translations.idiomatic: To squander the labor of ten thousand men on lavish spectacles is no way to burnish the throne's virtue or set an example for the realm."

sentences.zh: 乃止。

translations.literal: And so [the festivities] were halted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thereupon stopped them.

sentences.zh: 初，高麗既亡，其別種大祚榮徙居營州。

translations.literal: Initially, after Goguryeo had perished, a branch of its people, Da Zuorong, moved to Ying Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Goguryeo fell, a remnant of its people led by Da Zuorong resettled in Ying Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 及李盡忠反，祚榮與靺鞨乞四北羽聚眾東走，阻險自固。

translations.literal: When Li Jinzhong rebelled, Zuorong together with the Mohe leader Qi Sibeiyu gathered followers and fled east, holding difficult terrain to secure themselves.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Jinzhong rose in revolt, Zuorong and the Mohe chieftain Qi Sibeiyu rallied their bands and fled eastward, fortifying themselves in rugged country.

sentences.zh: 盡忠死，武後使將軍李楷固討其餘黨。

translations.literal: Jinzhong died; Empress Wu sent General Li Kaigu to destroy the remaining rebels.
translations.idiomatic: After Jinzhong's death, Empress Wu dispatched General Li Kaigu to hunt down the survivors.

sentences.zh: 楷固擊乞四北羽，斬之，引兵逾天門嶺，逼祚榮。

translations.literal: Kaigu attacked Qi Sibeiyu, killed him, led his troops over Tianmen Ridge, and pressed Zuorong.
translations.idiomatic: Kaigu struck Qi Sibeiyu and killed him, then crossed Tianmen Ridge and closed in on Zuorong.

sentences.zh: 祚榮逆戰，楷固大敗，僅以身免。

translations.literal: Zuorong counterattacked; Kaigu was badly defeated and barely escaped with his life.
translations.idiomatic: Zuorong met him in battle and routed him; Kaigu barely escaped alive.

sentences.zh: 祚榮遂帥其眾東據東牟山，築城居之。

translations.literal: Zuorong then led his followers east to occupy Dongmoushan, built a city, and settled there.
translations.idiomatic: Zuorong then led his people east to Dongmoushan, walled a city, and made it his seat.

sentences.zh: 祚榮驍勇善戰，高麗、靺鞨之人稍稍歸之，地方二千里，戶十餘萬，勝兵數萬人，自稱振國王，附於突厥。

translations.literal: Zuorong was fierce and skilled in battle; people of Goguryeo and Mohe gradually joined him. His domain covered two thousand li, with more than one hundred thousand households and several tens of thousands of fighting men. He styled himself King of Zhen and attached himself to the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: Bold and warlike, Zuorong drew Goguryeo and Mohe followers to him in growing numbers. His territory stretched two thousand li; households numbered more than a hundred thousand, and fighting men several tens of thousands. He proclaimed himself King of Zhen and submitted to the Turks.

sentences.zh: 時奚、契丹皆叛，道路阻絕，武後不能討。

translations.literal: At that time both the Xi and the Khitan had rebelled; the roads were cut off, and Empress Wu could not campaign against him.
translations.idiomatic: The Xi and Khitan were both in revolt, communications were severed, and Empress Wu could not reach him with an army.

sentences.zh: 中宗即位，遣侍御史張行岌招慰之，祚榮遣子入侍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhongzong took the throne, he sent Supervising Censor Zhang Xingji to summon and comfort him; Zuorong sent his son to attend court.
translations.idiomatic: On Zhongzong's accession he sent Supervising Censor Zhang Xingji to offer reassurance; Zuorong sent his son to serve at court.

sentences.zh: 至是，以祚榮為左驍衛大將軍、渤海郡王；

translations.literal: At this time Zuorong was appointed Left Cavalry Guard General and Prince of Bohai;
translations.idiomatic: Now Zuorong was made Left Cavalry Guard General and Prince of Bohai;

sentences.zh: 以其所部為忽汗州，令祚榮兼都督。

translations.literal: his followers were made into Huhan Prefecture, and Zuorong was made concurrently its governor.
translations.idiomatic: his people were organized as Huhan Prefecture, with Zuorong serving concurrently as governor.

sentences.zh: 庚申，敕以嚴挺之忠直宣示百官，厚賞之。

translations.literal: On gengshen, an edict announced Yan Tingzhi's loyalty and integrity to all officials, and he was richly rewarded.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen day an edict proclaimed Yan Tingzhi's loyalty and uprightness to the whole bureaucracy, and he received a generous reward.

sentences.zh: 三月，辛巳，皇后親蠶。

translations.literal: In the third month, on xinsi, the empress personally performed the sericulture rite.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on xinsi day, the empress personally tended the silkworms.

sentences.zh: 晉陵尉楊相如上疏言時政，其略曰：「煬帝自恃自強，不憂時政，雖制敕交行，而聲實舛謬，言同堯、舜，亦如桀、紂，舉天下之大，一擲而棄之。」

translations.literal: Yang Xiangru, magistrate of Jinling, submitted a memorial on current affairs; in summary he said: "Emperor Yang relied on his own strength, cared nothing for affairs of state; though edicts and orders issued one after another, word and reality were at odds—his speech matched Yao and Shun, yet his conduct matched Jie and Zhou; he took the whole realm and cast it away in a single throw."
translations.idiomatic: Jinling magistrate Yang Xiangru memorialized on affairs of the day. In essence he wrote: "Emperor Yang trusted only his own power and ignored governance. Edicts poured forth, yet words and deeds diverged—he spoke like Yao and Shun while acting like Jie and Zhou, and wagered the empire on a single reckless throw."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「隋氏縱欲而亡，太宗抑欲而昌，願陛下詳擇之！」

translations.literal: He also said: "The Sui indulged its desires and perished; Taizong restrained desire and flourished—Your Majesty, weigh these carefully!"
translations.idiomatic: He added: "The Sui dynasty drowned in excess and fell; Taizong checked his appetites and prospered. I beg Your Majesty to choose between these paths."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「人主莫不好忠正而惡佞邪，然忠正者常疏，佞邪者常親，以至於覆國危身而不寤者，何哉？

translations.literal: He also said: "No ruler fails to love the loyal and upright and hate the fawning and wicked—yet the loyal and upright are usually kept at a distance while the fawning and wicked are kept close, until states fall and lives are lost without awakening. Why is this?
translations.idiomatic: He went on: "Every sovereign favors loyalty and detests flattery—yet the loyal are pushed away and sycophants embraced, until realm and ruler are ruined without a change of heart. Why?

sentences.zh: 誠由忠正者多忤意，佞邪者多順指，積忤生憎，積順生愛，此親疏之所以分也。

translations.literal: Truly it is because the loyal and upright often offend one's wishes while the fawning and wicked often accord with one's inclinations; accumulated offense breeds hatred, accumulated compliance breeds affection—this is why closeness and distance divide.
translations.idiomatic: Because the upright speak against the ruler's wishes and flatterers echo them. Offense piled up breeds dislike; compliance piled up breeds fondness—that is how favor and exile are sorted.

sentences.zh: 明主則不然。

translations.literal: An enlightened ruler is not like this.
translations.idiomatic: A wise sovereign does otherwise.

sentences.zh: 愛其忤以收忠賢，惡其順以去佞邪，則太宗太平之業，將何遠哉！」

translations.literal: Cherish those who offend in order to gather the loyal and worthy; hate those who comply in order to remove the fawning and wicked—then how far could Taizong's age of peace be!"
translations.idiomatic: Welcome contradiction to win true servants; reject smooth agreement to purge sycophants—then Taizong's peace would be near at hand."

sentences.zh: 又曰「夫法貴簡而能禁，罰貴輕而必行；

translations.literal: He also said: "Law should be valued for simplicity yet able to restrain; punishment should be valued for lightness yet sure to be enforced;
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: "Good law is simple yet binding; good punishment is light yet inevitable—

sentences.zh: 陛下方興崇至德，大布新政，請一切除去碎密，不察小過。

translations.literal: Your Majesty is now raising supreme virtue and spreading great new policies—please abolish altogether petty and minute regulations and do not scrutinize small faults.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is proclaiming supreme virtue and sweeping reforms. Abolish petty rules and stop policing minor slips.

sentences.zh: 小過不察則無煩苛，大罪不漏則止奸慝，使簡而難犯，寬而能制，則善矣。」

translations.literal: If small faults are not scrutinized, there will be no vexatious severity; if great crimes are not overlooked, wickedness will be stopped—make law simple yet hard to violate, lenient yet able to control, and that will be good.
translations.idiomatic: Overlook small faults and bureaucracy loses its bite; miss no grave crime and villainy is checked. Law that is simple to grasp yet hard to break, and clemency that still holds the line—that is the ideal."

sentences.zh: 上覽而善之。

translations.literal: The emperor read it and approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read the memorial and was pleased.

sentences.zh: 先是，修大明宮未畢，夏，五月，庚寅，敕以農務方勤，罷之以待閒月。

translations.literal: Earlier, construction of the Daming Palace had not been finished; in summer, in the fifth month, on gengyin, an edict held that farm work was then pressing and suspended the project to await a slack season.
translations.idiomatic: The Daming Palace was still unfinished. In the fifth month, on gengyin day in summer, an edict halted work until the farming season eased.

sentences.zh: 六月，丙辰，以兵部尚書郭元振同中書門下三品。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on bingchen, Minister of War Guo Yuanzhen was made Associate of the Three Departments of the Secretariat and Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on bingchen day, Minister of War Guo Yuanzhen was appointed Associate of the Three Departments.

sentences.zh: 太平公主依上皇之勢，擅權用事，與上有隙，宰相七人，五出其門。

translations.literal: Princess Taiping relied on the Retired Emperor's power, monopolized authority and handled affairs, had a rift with the emperor, and of seven chancellors five came from her faction.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Taiping leaned on the Retired Emperor's backing, seized power, and fell out with the emperor. Five of seven chancellors were her clients.

sentences.zh: 文武之臣，太半附之。

translations.literal: More than half of civil and military ministers attached themselves to her.
translations.idiomatic: Well over half the court, civil and military alike, lined up behind her.

sentences.zh: 與竇懷貞、岑羲、蕭至忠、崔湜及太子少保薛稷、雍州長史新興王晉、左羽林大將軍常元楷、知右羽林將軍事李慈、左金吾將軍李欽、中書舍人李猷、右散騎常侍賈膺福、鴻臚卿唐晙及僧慧范等謀廢立，又與宮人元氏謀於赤箭粉中置毒進於上。

translations.literal: Together with Dou Huaizhen, Cen Xi, Xiao Zhizhong, Cui Shi, and Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent Xue Ji, Chief Administrator of Yong Prefecture Prince Jin of Xinxing, Left General of the Feathered Forest Guard Chang Yuankai, Acting Right General of the Feathered Forest Guard Li Ci, Left Golden Guard General Li Qin, Secretariat Drafting Officer Li You, Right Regular Attendant Jia Yingfu, Chamberlain for Dependencies Tang Jun, and the monk Huifan and others she plotted deposition and enthronement; she also conspired with palace woman Lady Yuan to place poison in arrowroot powder and present it to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: With Dou Huaizhen, Cen Xi, Xiao Zhizhong, Cui Shi, Heir Apparent Grand Mentor Xue Ji, Yong Prefecture chief administrator Prince Jin of Xinxing, Left Feathered Forest General Chang Yuankai, acting Right Feathered Forest commander Li Ci, Left Golden Guard General Li Qin, drafting officer Li You, Right Regular Attendant Jia Yingfu, Chamberlain for Dependencies Tang Jun, and the monk Huifan she plotted to depose the emperor and raise another. With the palace woman Lady Yuan she also schemed to lace arrowroot powder with poison and serve it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 晉，德良之孫也。

translations.literal: Jin was the grandson of Deliang.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jin was a grandson of Deliang.

sentences.zh: 元楷、慈數往來主第，相與結謀。

translations.literal: Yuankai and Ci frequently came and went at the princess's mansion, joining together in conspiracy.
translations.idiomatic: Yuankai and Ci shuttled in and out of the princess's residence, plotting together.

sentences.zh: 王琚言於上曰：「事迫矣，不可不速發！」

translations.literal: Wang Ju said to the emperor: 'The matter is urgent—You cannot fail to act quickly!'
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ju told the emperor, 'This has gone too far—you must strike at once.'

sentences.zh: 左丞張說自東都遣人遺上佩刀，意欲上斷割。

translations.literal: Left Assistant Director Zhang Yue sent a man from the Eastern Capital to present the emperor with a girdle knife, intending that the emperor cut and decide.
translations.idiomatic: From Luoyang, Left Assistant Director Zhang Yue sent the emperor a belt knife—a signal to cut the knot.

sentences.zh: 荊州長史崔日用入奏事，言於上曰：「太平謀逆有日，陛下往在東宮，猶為臣子，若欲討之，須用謀力。

translations.literal: Jing Prefecture chief administrator Cui Riyong entered to report on affairs and said to the emperor: 'Princess Taiping has long plotted rebellion. When Your Majesty was still in the Eastern Palace you were yet a subject; to move against her would have required stratagem and force.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhou chief administrator Cui Riyong came to audience and warned the emperor: 'The princess has been plotting treason for some time. When you were still crown prince you were only a subject; to strike her then would have taken cunning and armed strength.

sentences.zh: 今既光臨大寶，但下一制書，誰敢不從？

translations.literal: Now that you have ascended the great treasure, you need only issue a single edict—who would dare not obey?
translations.idiomatic: Now you sit on the throne. One edict is enough—who would refuse?

sentences.zh: 萬一奸宄得志，悔之何及！」

translations.literal: If by any chance the traitors succeed, how could you regret it in time!'
translations.idiomatic: If the plotters win, regret will come too late.'

sentences.zh: 上曰：「誠如卿言。

translations.literal: The emperor said: 'It is truly as you say.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, 'You are right.

sentences.zh: 直恐驚動上皇。」

translations.literal: I only fear alarming the Retired Emperor.'
translations.idiomatic: I only fear upsetting the Retired Emperor.'

sentences.zh: 日用曰：「天子之孝在於安四海。

translations.literal: Riyong said: 'The filial piety of the Son of Heaven lies in securing the four seas.
translations.idiomatic: Riyong replied, 'A son of Heaven shows filial piety by securing the realm.

sentences.zh: 若奸人得志，則社稷為墟，安在其為孝乎！」

translations.literal: If wicked men succeed, then the altars of state become ruins—in what sense would that be filial!'
translations.idiomatic: If traitors prevail the altars lie in ruins—where is the filiality in that?'

sentences.zh: 請先定北軍，後收逆黨，則不驚動上皇矣。

translations.literal: Please first secure the Northern Army, then seize the rebel faction—then the Retired Emperor will not be alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: Secure the Northern Army first, then round up the rebels—the Retired Emperor need never be disturbed.

sentences.zh: 上以為然。

translations.literal: The emperor thought this right.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 以日用為吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: Riyong was appointed Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Riyong was made Vice Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，魏知古告公主欲以是月四日作亂，令元楷、慈以羽林兵突入武德殿，懷貞、至忠、羲等於南牙舉兵應之。

translations.literal: In autumn, in the seventh month, Wei Zhigu reported that the princess intended to rebel on the fourth of that month, ordering Yuankai and Ci to lead Feathered Forest troops in a sudden entry into Wude Hall while Huaizhen, Zhizhong, Xi, and the others would raise troops at the Southern Compound in support.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn, Wei Zhigu reported that the princess planned a coup on the fourth, with Yuankai and Ci to burst into Wude Hall at the head of Feathered Forest troops while Huaizhen, Zhizhong, Xi, and their allies mustered forces at the Southern Compound.

sentences.zh: 上乃與岐王范、薛王業、郭元振及龍武將軍王毛仲、殿中少監姜皎、太僕少卿李令問、尚乘奉御王守一、內給事高力士、果毅李守德等定計誅之。

translations.literal: The emperor then joined with Princes Fan of Qi and Ye of Xue, Guo Yuanzhen, and Longwu General Wang Maoqi, Palace Supervisor Assistant Jiang Jiao, Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud Li Lingwen, Palace Stud Attendant Wang Shouyi, Inner Palace Supply Officer Gao Lishi, and Guardsman Li Shoude and others to fix a plan to execute them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then plotted with Princes Fan of Qi and Ye of Xue, Guo Yuanzhen, Longwu General Wang Maozhong, Palace Supervisor Assistant Jiang Jiao, Court of the Imperial Stud vice minister Li Lingwen, Palace Stud attendant Wang Shouyi, inner palace supply officer Gao Lishi, guardsman Li Shoude, and others to kill the conspirators.

sentences.zh: 皎，謨之曾孫；

translations.literal: Jiao was a great-grandson of Mo;
translations.idiomatic: Jiao was a great-grandson of Mo.

sentences.zh: 令問，靖弟客師之孫；

translations.literal: Lingwen was a grandson of Jing's younger brother Keshi;
translations.idiomatic: Lingwen was a grandson of Li Jing's younger brother Keshi.

sentences.zh: 守一，仁皎之子；

translations.literal: Shouyi was the son of Renjiao;
translations.idiomatic: Shouyi was the son of Wang Renjiao.

sentences.zh: 力士，潘州人也。

translations.literal: Lishi was a man of Pan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Lishi came from Pan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 甲子，上因王毛仲取閒廄馬及兵三百餘人，與同謀十餘人，自武德殿入虔化門，召元楷、慈，先斬之，擒膺福、猷於內客省以出，執至忠、羲於朝堂，皆斬之。

translations.literal: On jiazi, the emperor through Wang Maoqi took spare-stable horses and more than three hundred soldiers, together with more than ten fellow conspirators, entered from Wude Hall through Qianhua Gate, summoned Yuankai and Ci, and beheaded them first; he seized Yingfu and You in the Inner Reception Office and brought them out, arrested Zhizhong and Xi in the audience hall, and beheaded them all.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi day the emperor, through Wang Maozhong, took three hundred-odd spare-stable horses and soldiers plus a dozen co-conspirators, left Wude Hall for Qianhua Gate, summoned Yuankai and Ci and cut them down first, seized Yingfu and You in the Inner Reception Office, dragged Zhizhong and Xi from the audience hall, and executed them all.

sentences.zh: 懷貞逃入溝中，自縊死，戮其屍，改姓曰毒。

translations.literal: Huaizhen fled into a ditch and hanged himself; his corpse was mutilated and his surname changed to Du [Poison].
translations.idiomatic: Huaizhen fled into a drainage ditch and hanged himself. His corpse was mutilated and his clan name changed to Du—'Poison.'

sentences.zh: 上皇聞變，登承天門樓。

translations.literal: The Retired Emperor heard of the upheaval and mounted Chengtian Gate tower.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of the coup, the Retired Emperor climbed Chengtian Gate tower.

sentences.zh: 郭元振奏，皇帝前奉誥誅竇懷貞等，無他也。

translations.literal: Guo Yuanzhen reported: 'The emperor has just now, by edict, executed Dou Huaizhen and the others—nothing more.'
translations.idiomatic: Guo Yuanzhen announced, 'The emperor has just executed Dou Huaizhen and his fellows by imperial order—nothing beyond that.'

sentences.zh: 上尋至樓上，上皇乃下誥罪狀懷貞等，因赦天下，惟逆人親黨不赦。

translations.literal: The emperor soon came to the tower; the Retired Emperor then issued an edict listing the crimes of Huaizhen and the others, and thereupon pardoned the realm, except that the relatives and partisans of rebels were not pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor soon joined him on the tower. The Retired Emperor issued an edict enumerating Huaizhen's crimes, then proclaimed a general amnesty—rebel kin and accomplices excepted.

sentences.zh: 薛稷賜死於萬年獄。

translations.literal: Xue Ji was granted death in Wannian Prison.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Ji was ordered to take his own life in Wannian Prison.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，上皇誥：「自今軍國政刑，一皆取皇帝處分。

translations.literal: On yichou, the Retired Emperor issued an edict: 'From now on all military and civil affairs, punishments and government, shall entirely be decided by the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou day the Retired Emperor decreed: 'Henceforth every matter of war, state, law, and governance rests with the emperor.

sentences.zh: 朕方無為養志，以遂素心。」

translations.literal: I shall practice nonaction and nourish my will, to fulfill my lifelong wish.'
translations.idiomatic: I shall retire from affairs and tend my peace, as I have always wished.'

sentences.zh: 是日，徙居百福殿。

translations.literal: That day he moved to Baifu Hall.
translations.idiomatic: That same day he moved into Baifu Hall.

sentences.zh: 太平公主逃入山寺，三日乃出，賜死於家，公主諸子及黨與死者數十人。

translations.literal: Princess Taiping fled into a mountain monastery; after three days she came out, was granted death at home, and several tens of the princess's sons and partisans died.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Taiping hid in a mountain temple. After three days she emerged, was ordered to die at home, and dozens of her sons and followers perished with her faction.

sentences.zh: 薛崇簡以數諫其母被撻，特免死，賜姓李，官爵如故。

translations.literal: Xue Chongjian, because he had repeatedly remonstrated with his mother and been flogged, was specially spared death, granted the surname Li, and his office and rank remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Chongjian, who had often warned his mother and been beaten for it, was spared, given the surname Li, and kept his titles.

sentences.zh: 籍公主家，財貨山積，珍物侔於御府，廄牧羊馬、田園息錢，收之數年不盡。

translations.literal: The princess's household was inventoried; wealth piled like mountains, rare goods rivaling the imperial storehouse; stables of sheep and horses and estate interest-money—collecting them fully would take years.
translations.idiomatic: Her estate was seized. Treasure heaped like hills; curios matched the imperial vaults. Livestock, pastures, and interest from landholdings—years would not exhaust what was there.

sentences.zh: 慧范家產亦數十萬緡。

translations.literal: Huifan's household property also amounted to several hundred thousand strings of cash.
translations.idiomatic: Huifan's holdings too ran to several hundred thousand strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 改新興王晉之姓曰厲。

translations.literal: Prince Jin of Xinxing had his surname changed to Li [Cruel].
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jin of Xinxing had his clan name changed to Li—'Cruel.'

sentences.zh: 初，上謀誅竇懷貞等，召崔湜，將托以心腹。

translations.literal: Initially, when the emperor plotted to execute Dou Huaizhen and the others, he summoned Cui Shi, intending to entrust him as a confidant.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while planning to kill Dou Huaizhen and his circle, the emperor summoned Cui Shi intending to make him a trusted insider.

sentences.zh: 湜弟滌謂湜曰：「主上有問，勿有所隱。」

translations.literal: Shi's younger brother Di said to Shi: 'If the sovereign questions you, do not conceal anything.'
translations.idiomatic: Shi's brother Di urged him: 'If the emperor asks, hide nothing.'

sentences.zh: 湜不從。

translations.literal: Shi did not follow this.
translations.idiomatic: Shi refused.

sentences.zh: 懷貞等既誅，湜與右丞盧藏用俱坐私侍太平公主，湜流竇州，藏用流瀧州。

translations.literal: After Huaizhen and the others had been executed, Shi together with Right Assistant Director Lu Zangyong were both convicted of privately attending Princess Taiping; Shi was exiled to Dou Prefecture, Zangyong to Long Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Once Huaizhen's faction was dead, Shi and Right Assistant Director Lu Zangyong were punished for secretly serving the princess. Shi was banished to Dou Prefecture, Zangyong to Long Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 新興王晉臨刑歎曰：「本為此謀者崔湜，今吾死湜生，不亦冤乎！」

translations.literal: Prince Jin of Xinxing at execution sighed: 'The one who truly plotted this was Cui Shi—now I die while Shi lives. Is that not unjust!'
translations.idiomatic: Facing execution, Prince Jin of Xinxing cried, 'Cui Shi hatched this plot—yet I die and he lives. Where is the justice in that?'

sentences.zh: 會有司鞫宮人元氏，元氏引湜同謀進毒，乃追賜死於荊州。

translations.literal: Just then the authorities interrogated the palace woman Lady Yuan; Yuan implicated Shi in the joint plot to present poison, and he was recalled and granted death at Jing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Then investigators examined the palace woman Lady Yuan, who named Shi as her co-conspirator in the poisoning. He was recalled and ordered to die at Jing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 薛稷之子伯陽以尚主免死，流嶺南，於道自殺。

translations.literal: Xue Ji's son Boyang, because he had married an imperial princess, was spared death and exiled to Lingnan; on the road he killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Ji's son Boyang, spared because he had married a princess, was sent to Lingnan and killed himself on the way.

sentences.zh: 初，太平公主與其黨謀廢立，竇懷貞、蕭至忠、岑羲、崔湜皆以為然，陸象先獨以為不可。

translations.literal: Initially, when Princess Taiping and her faction plotted deposition and enthronement, Dou Huaizhen, Xiao Zhizhong, Cen Xi, and Cui Shi all agreed; Lu Xiangxian alone held it impossible.
translations.idiomatic: When the princess and her allies first plotted to depose the emperor, Huaizhen, Zhizhong, Cen Xi, and Cui Shi all assented—only Lu Xiangxian refused.

sentences.zh: 公主曰：「廢長立少，已為不順；

translations.literal: The princess said: 'To depose the elder and establish the younger is already unfilial;
translations.idiomatic: The princess argued: 'Replacing the elder with the younger is already wrong;

sentences.zh: 且又失德，若之何不去？」

translations.literal: moreover he has lost virtue—why not remove him?'
translations.idiomatic: and besides, he lacks virtue—why keep him?'

sentences.zh: 象先曰：「既以功立，當以罪廢。

translations.literal: Xiangxian said: 'Since he was established for his merit, he should be deposed for his crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangxian replied: 'If merit raised him, crime should remove him.

sentences.zh: 今實無罪，像先終不敢從。」

translations.literal: Now he is in truth without crime—Xiangxian ultimately dares not follow.'
translations.idiomatic: But he has committed no crime. I cannot go along.'

sentences.zh: 公主怒而去。

translations.literal: The princess left in anger.
translations.idiomatic: The princess stormed off.

sentences.zh: 上既誅懷貞等，召象先謂曰：「歲寒知松柏，信哉！」

translations.literal: After the emperor had executed Huaizhen and the others, he summoned Xiangxian and said: 'Only in cold weather do we know pine and cypress—how true!'
translations.idiomatic: After Huaizhen's faction was destroyed the emperor summoned Xiangxian and said, 'Cold weather reveals the pine and cypress—truer words were never spoken.'

sentences.zh: 時窮治公主枝黨，當坐者眾，像先密為申理，所全甚多；

translations.literal: At that time the princess's partisans were being thoroughly prosecuted; many were liable to punishment, and Xiangxian secretly pleaded on their behalf—those he preserved were many;
translations.idiomatic: With the princess's network under relentless prosecution, Xiangxian quietly interceded for many who would otherwise have fallen;

sentences.zh: 然未嘗自言，當時無知者。

translations.literal: yet he never spoke of it himself, and at the time none knew.
translations.idiomatic: yet he never claimed credit, and no one knew.

sentences.zh: 百官素為公主所善及惡之者，或黜或陟，終歲不盡。

translations.literal: Officials whom the princess had favored or hated were demoted or promoted in turn—the work was not finished within the year.
translations.idiomatic: Officials the princess had favored or despised were promoted or cashiered in turn—a year's work did not clear the backlog.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，上御承天門樓，赦天下。

translations.literal: On dingmao, the emperor mounted Chengtian Gate tower and pardoned the realm.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao day the emperor ascended Chengtian Gate tower and proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 己巳，賞功臣郭元振等官爵、第捨、金帛有差。

translations.literal: On jisi, meritorious officials including Guo Yuanzhen were rewarded with offices and ranks, mansions, gold, and silk in varying measure.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi day the emperor rewarded Guo Yuanzhen and other loyalists with titles, estates, gold, and silk according to their deserts.

sentences.zh: 以高力士為右監門將軍，知內侍省事。

translations.literal: Gao Lishi was made Right General of the Gate Guards and placed in charge of the Palace Domestic Service.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Lishi was appointed Right Gate Guard General and put in charge of the Palace Domestic Service.

sentences.zh: 初，太宗定制，內侍省不置三品官，黃衣廩食，守門傳命而已。

translations.literal: Initially, Taizong established the rule that the Palace Domestic Service would not appoint third-rank officials; [eunuchs wore] yellow robes, received grain rations, and merely guarded gates and relayed orders.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong had decreed that the Palace Domestic Service would appoint no third-rank officers: eunuchs wore yellow, drew rations, and merely kept gates and carried orders.

sentences.zh: 天後雖女主，宦官亦不用事。

translations.literal: Though Empress Wu was a woman sovereign, eunuchs also did not handle affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Even under Empress Wu, eunuchs held no power.

sentences.zh: 中宗時，嬖倖猥多，宦官七品以上至千餘人，然衣緋者尚寡。

translations.literal: In Emperor Zhongzong's time favored attendants were numerous and base; eunuchs of seventh rank and above reached more than a thousand, yet those wearing scarlet were still few.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhongzong favorites multiplied and eunuchs of seventh rank or higher numbered over a thousand, though few yet wore scarlet.

sentences.zh: 上在籓邸，力士傾心奉之，及為太子，奏為內給事，至是以誅蕭、岑功賞之。

translations.literal: When the emperor was in his princely residence, Lishi devoted himself to serving him; when he became heir apparent, [Lishi] was memorialized as inner palace supply officer—to this point he was rewarded for the merit of executing Xiao and Cen.
translations.idiomatic: While the emperor was still a prince, Lishi served him wholeheartedly; when he became heir apparent Lishi was made inner palace supply officer—and now was rewarded for helping bring down Xiao and Cen.

sentences.zh: 是後宦官稍增至三千餘人，除三品將軍者浸多，衣緋、紫至千餘人，宦官之盛自此始。

translations.literal: After this eunuchs gradually increased to more than three thousand; those appointed third-rank generals grew ever more numerous, and those wearing scarlet and purple reached more than a thousand—the eunuchs' ascendancy began from this.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter eunuchs swelled to more than three thousand. Third-rank generalships multiplied; scarlet and purple robes numbered over a thousand. Eunuch power dates from this moment.

sentences.zh: 壬申，遣益州長史畢構等六人宣撫十道。

translations.literal: On renshen, Bi Gou, chief administrator of Yi Prefecture, and five others were dispatched to proclaim reassurance through the ten circuits.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen day Bi Gou of Yi Prefecture and five others were sent to pacify and reassure the ten circuits.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，以左丞張說為中書令。

translations.literal: On yihai, Left Assistant Director Zhang Yue was made Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai day Left Assistant Director Zhang Yue became Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，中書侍郎、同平章事陸象先罷為益州長史、劍南按察使。

translations.literal: On gengchen, Secretariat Vice Director and Associate Director Lu Xiangxian was removed and made chief administrator of Yi Prefecture and Inspector of Jiannan.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen day Secretariat Vice Director and Associate Director Lu Xiangxian was dismissed to serve as chief administrator of Yi Prefecture and Jiannan inspector.

sentences.zh: 八月，癸巳，以封州流人劉幽求為左僕射、平章軍國大事。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on guisi, the exiled Liu Youqiu of Feng Prefecture was made Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and Associate Director for Military and State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on guisi day, the Feng Prefecture exile Liu Youqiu was recalled as Left Vice Director and Associate Director for Military and State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，突厥可汗默啜遣其子楊我支來求昏；

translations.literal: On bingchen, Moqie, khan of the Turks, sent his son Yang Wozhi to request marriage;
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen day Turkic khan Moqie sent his son Yang Wozhi to sue for a bride;

sentences.zh: 丁巳，許以蜀王女南和縣主妻之。

translations.literal: on dingsi, [the court] agreed to give him the Princess of Nanhe, daughter of the Prince of Shu, as wife.
translations.idiomatic: on dingsi day the court agreed to marry him to Princess Nanhe, daughter of the Prince of Shu.

sentences.zh: 中宗之崩也，同中書門下三品李嶠密表韋後，請出相王諸子於外。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhongzong died, Li Jiao, Associate of the Three Departments, secretly memorialized Empress Wei requesting that the Prince of Xiang's sons be sent outside [the capital].
translations.idiomatic: At Zhongzong's death Li Jiao, Associate of the Three Departments, secretly urged Empress Wei to send the Prince of Xiang's sons out of the capital.

sentences.zh: 上即位，於禁中得其表，以示侍臣。

translations.literal: When the emperor took the throne, he found the memorial in the inner palace and showed it to attending ministers.
translations.idiomatic: On his own accession the emperor found that memorial in the palace archives and showed it to his ministers.

sentences.zh: 嶠時以特進致仕，或請誅之，張說曰：「嶠雖不識逆順，然為當時之謀則忠矣。」

translations.literal: Jiao was then retired with the special emeritus rank; some requested his execution, but Zhang Yue said: 'Though Jiao did not discern rebellion from loyalty, for the plotting of that time he was loyal.'
translations.idiomatic: Jiao was then retired as Special Emeritus. Some urged his execution, but Zhang Yue said, 'He misread the tide of events, yet for that moment his counsel was loyal.'

sentences.zh: 上然之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 九月，壬戌，以嶠子率更令暢為虔州刺史，令嶠隨暢之官。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on renxu, Jiao's son Chang, Director of the Palace Revisions Office, was made prefect of Qian Prefecture, and Jiao was ordered to accompany Chang to his post.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on renxu day, Jiao's son Chang, Director of the Palace Revisions Office, was appointed prefect of Qianzhou, and Jiao was bidden to join him in taking up the post.

sentences.zh: 庚午，以劉幽求同中書門下三品。

translations.literal: On gengwu, Liu Youqiu was made Associate of the Three Departments of the Secretariat and Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu day, Liu Youqiu was appointed Associate of the Three Departments.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，復置右御史台，督察諸州，罷諸道按察使。

translations.literal: On bingxu, the Right Censorate was re-established to inspect the prefectures, and the circuit inspecting commissioners of all circuits were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu day the Right Censorate was restored to oversee the prefectures, and the circuit inspecting commissioners were abolished.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，辛卯，引見京畿縣令，戒以歲饑惠養黎元之意。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on xinmao, he summoned the county magistrates of the capital region and admonished them with his intent to care for the common people amid famine.
