translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter, on xinmao day, he received the county magistrates of the capital region and urged them to nurture the people through the year's famine.

sentences.zh: 己亥，上幸新豐；

translations.literal: On jihai, the emperor visited Xinfeng;
translations.idiomatic: On jihai day the emperor traveled to Xinfeng;

sentences.zh: 癸卯，講武於驪山之下，徵兵二十萬，旌旗連亙五十餘里。

translations.literal: On guimao, he conducted military exercises below Mount Li, mobilizing two hundred thousand troops; banners and flags stretched in unbroken succession for more than fifty li.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao day he held a martial review below Mount Li, mustering two hundred thousand men; banners and standards lined the field for more than fifty li.

sentences.zh: 以軍容不整，坐兵部尚書郭元振於纛下，將斬之。

translations.literal: Because the troops' bearing was not orderly, he seated Minister of War Guo Yuanzhen beneath the command banner and was about to execute him.
translations.idiomatic: Finding the army's formation slack, he had Minister of War Guo Yuanzhen placed beneath the command banner and prepared to behead him.

sentences.zh: 劉幽求、張說跪於馬前諫曰：「元振有大功於社稷，不可殺。」

translations.literal: Liu Youqiu and Zhang Shuo knelt before the horse and remonstrated, saying, "Yuanzhen has great merit to the altars of state; he must not be killed."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Youqiu and Zhang Shuo knelt before the imperial horse and pleaded: "Yuanzhen has served the realm with great merit — he cannot be put to death."

sentences.zh: 乃流新州。

translations.literal: Thereupon [Yuanzhen] was exiled to Xin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhen was thereupon banished to Xinzhou.

sentences.zh: 斬給事中、知禮儀事唐紹，以其制軍禮不肅故也。

translations.literal: Attendant-in-ordinary Tang Shao, overseer of ritual matters, was executed because his regulation of military ceremony lacked solemnity.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant-in-ordinary Tang Shao, who oversaw ritual protocol, was beheaded for failing to keep the military rites in proper order.

sentences.zh: 上始欲立威，亦無殺紹之意，金吾衛將軍李邈遽宣敕斬之。

translations.literal: The emperor had at first wished to establish awe and had no intention of killing Shao, but General of the Jinwu Guard Li Miao hastily proclaimed the edict and had him executed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had meant only to assert his authority and had no wish to kill Shao, but Jinwu Guard General Li Miao abruptly announced the decree and had him cut down.

sentences.zh: 上尋罷邈官，廢棄終身。

translations.literal: The emperor soon removed Miao from office and discarded him for life.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor soon stripped Miao of his post and cast him aside for the rest of his days.

sentences.zh: 時二大臣得罪，諸軍多震懾失次，惟左軍節度薛訥、朔方道大總管解琬二軍不動，上遣輕騎召之，皆不得入其陳。

translations.literal: At that time, with two great ministers having offended, many armies were shaken and lost formation; only the armies of Left Army commander Xue Ne and Shuofang circuit Grand general Jie Wan held firm. The emperor sent light cavalry to summon them, but none could enter their arrays.
translations.idiomatic: With two senior ministers now disgraced, most units quailed and fell out of rank; only the divisions under Left Army commander Xue Ne and Shuofang circuit Grand general Jie Wan held steady. The emperor sent light horsemen to call them in, yet none could penetrate their formations.

sentences.zh: 上深歎美，慰勉之。

translations.literal: The emperor deeply sighed in admiration and comforted and encouraged them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sighed in deep admiration and praised and encouraged them.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，獵於渭川。

translations.literal: On jiachen, he hunted at Weichuan.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen day he hunted along the Wei River.

sentences.zh: 上欲以同州刺史姚元之為相，張說疾之，使御史大夫趙彥昭彈之，上不納。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to appoint Tong Prefecture Governor Yao Yuanzhi as chancellor; Zhang Shuo resented this and had Censor-in-chief Zhao Yanzhao impeach him, but the emperor did not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to make Tongzhou Governor Yao Yuanzhi chancellor; Zhang Shuo, who resented him, had Censor-in-chief Zhao Yanzhao bring charges, but the emperor would not heed them.

sentences.zh: 又使殿中監姜皎言於上曰：「陛下常欲擇河東總管而難其人，臣今得之矣。」

translations.literal: He also had Palace Steward Jiang Jiao speak to the emperor, saying, "Your Majesty has often wished to choose someone as Hedong area commander but found no suitable man; I have found him now."
translations.idiomatic: He also had Palace Steward Jiang Jiao tell the emperor, "Your Majesty has long sought a worthy Hedong area commander without finding one — I have the man now."

sentences.zh: 上問為誰，皎曰：「姚元之文武全才，真其人也。」

translations.literal: The emperor asked who it was; Jiang said, "Yao Yuanzhi is a man of complete civil and military talent — truly the one."
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor asked who, Jiang replied, "Yao Yuanzhi combines civil and military excellence — he is the man."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「此張說之意也，汝何得面欺，罪當死！」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "This is Zhang Shuo's idea; how dare you deceive me to my face — the penalty should be death!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "This is Zhang Shuo's scheme. How dare you lie to my face — the punishment is death!"

sentences.zh: 皎叩頭首服，上即遣中使召元之詣行在。

translations.literal: Jiang kowtowed and confessed; the emperor immediately dispatched a palace emissary to summon Yuanzhi to the imperial traveling residence.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang kowtowed and admitted his guilt; the emperor at once sent a palace envoy to summon Yuanzhi to the imperial camp.

sentences.zh: 既至，上方獵，引見，即拜兵部尚書、同中書門下三品。

translations.literal: Once he arrived, the emperor was still hunting; he received him in audience and immediately appointed him Minister of War and Associate of the Three Departments.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuanzhi arrived the emperor was still out hunting; he received him on the spot and immediately named him Minister of War and Associate of the Three Departments.

sentences.zh: 元之吏事明敏，三為宰相，皆兼兵部尚書，緣邊屯戍斥候，士馬儲械，無不默記。

translations.literal: Yuanzhi was clear and sharp in administrative affairs; thrice he served as chancellor, each time concurrently holding the post of Minister of War — border garrisons, scouts, troops, horses, stored weapons: none escaped his silent memorization.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhi was quick and exact in office. Three times he served as chancellor, each time also holding the Ministry of War; frontier garrisons, outposts, men, horses, and stores of arms — he committed them all to memory without effort.

sentences.zh: 上初即位，勵精為治，每事訪於元之。

translations.literal: When the emperor first took the throne, he applied himself diligently to governance and consulted Yuanzhi on every matter.
translations.idiomatic: In the early days of his reign the emperor threw himself into government and consulted Yuanzhi on every affair.

sentences.zh: 元之應答如響，同僚皆唯諾而已，故上專委任之。

translations.literal: Yuanzhi answered like an echo; his colleagues merely nodded assent, and so the emperor entrusted affairs to him exclusively.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhi answered at once; his fellow ministers could only assent, and the emperor came to rely on him alone.

sentences.zh: 元之請抑權幸，愛爵賞，納諫諍，卻貢獻，不與群臣褻狎；

translations.literal: Yuanzhi requested that favor and power be checked, honors and rewards cherished, remonstrance welcomed, tribute gifts refused, and that the emperor not be overly familiar with his officials.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhi urged him to curb the privileged, value rank and reward, heed frank counsel, reject lavish tribute, and keep a proper distance from his ministers.

sentences.zh: 上皆納之。

translations.literal: The emperor accepted all of it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted every recommendation.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，車駕還京師。

translations.literal: On yisi, the imperial carriage returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi day the imperial procession returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 姚元之嘗奏請序進郎吏，上仰視殿屋，元之再三言之，終不應；

translations.literal: Yao Yuanzhi once memorialized requesting the orderly promotion of bureau clerks; the emperor looked up at the hall rafters; Yuanzhi spoke repeatedly, but in the end received no reply;
translations.idiomatic: Yao Yuanzhi once submitted a request to advance bureau clerks in due order; the emperor gazed up at the rafters of the hall. Yuanzhi pressed the matter again and again, but received no answer;

sentences.zh: 元之懼，趨出。

translations.literal: Yuanzhi was afraid and hurried out.
translations.idiomatic: Alarmed, Yuanzhi withdrew in haste.

sentences.zh: 罷朝，高力士諫曰：「陛下新總萬機，宰臣奏事，當面加可否，奈何一不省察！」

translations.literal: After court was dismissed, Gao Lishi remonstrated, saying, "Your Majesty has newly assumed all affairs of state; when the chief minister reports business, you ought to affirm or reject it to his face — how can you pay no heed whatsoever!"
translations.idiomatic: When court adjourned, Gao Lishi advised him: "Your Majesty has only just taken the reins of government. When the chief minister reports, you should answer yes or no on the spot — how can you ignore him entirely!"

sentences.zh: 上曰：「朕任元之以庶政，大事當奏聞共議之；

translations.literal: The emperor said, "I have entrusted Yuanzhi with routine governance; great matters should be reported and jointly deliberated.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I have left routine administration to Yuanzhi. Major affairs should be brought to me for joint deliberation.

sentences.zh: 郎吏卑秩，乃一一以煩朕邪？」

translations.literal: Are low-ranking bureau clerks truly something to trouble me with one by one?"
translations.idiomatic: Must I be bothered with every petty clerk one by one?"

sentences.zh: 會力士宣事至省中，為元之道上語，元之乃喜。

translations.literal: When Lishi went to the Secretariat on palace business and relayed the emperor's words to Yuanzhi, Yuanzhi was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: When Lishi carried palace business to the Secretariat and repeated the emperor's words to Yuanzhi, Yuanzhi was greatly relieved.

sentences.zh: 聞者皆服上識君人之體。

translations.literal: Those who heard of it all admired the emperor's grasp of the proper way to govern people.
translations.idiomatic: All who heard of it admired the emperor's understanding of what it means to rule.

sentences.zh: 左拾遺曲江張九齡，以元之有重望，為上所信任，奏記勸其遠諂躁，進純厚，其略曰：「任人當才，為政大體，與之共理，無出此途。

translations.literal: Left Reminder Zhang Jiuling of Qujiang, because Yuanzhi enjoyed great standing and the emperor's trust, submitted a letter urging him to keep distance from flattery and impatience, and to advance the pure and substantial; in summary he wrote, "Appointing men according to talent is the great principle of governing; in shared administration there is no path beyond this.
translations.idiomatic: Left Reminder Zhang Jiuling of Qujiang, seeing Yuanzhi's high standing and the emperor's trust in him, sent a letter urging him to shun sycophants and the restless, and to promote the steady and sincere. Its gist ran: "To appoint men by talent is the foundation of government; in ruling together there is no better course.

sentences.zh: 而向之用才，非無知人之鑒，其所以失溺，在緣情之舉。」

translations.literal: Yet in past appointments of talent, though he was not without discernment in knowing men, what led him to drown was choosing on the basis of personal feeling.
translations.idiomatic: In your past appointments you were not without an eye for men; what ruined you was choosing by affection rather than merit."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「自君侯職相國之重，持用人之權，而淺中弱植之徒，已延頸企踵而至，諂親戚以求譽，媚賓客以取容，其間豈不有才，所失在於無恥。」

translations.literal: He also wrote, "Since you, Lord, hold the weight of the chancellor's office and wield the power of appointment, shallow men of weak character have already craned their necks and lifted their heels to arrive — flattering relatives to seek praise, fawning on guests to win favor; among them there are certainly men of talent, but what is lost lies in their lack of shame."
translations.idiomatic: He added: "Since you bear the chancellor's burden and hold the power of appointment, shallow and spineless men are already craning their necks to reach you — flattering kin for praise, courting guests for favor. Some may indeed have talent; what is lost is their shamelessness."

sentences.zh: 元之嘉納其言。

translations.literal: Yuanzhi gladly accepted his words.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhi welcomed his counsel.

sentences.zh: 新興王晉之誅也，僚吏皆奔散，惟司功李摠步從，不失在官之禮，仍哭其屍。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Xinxing Jin was executed, his staff officials all fled; only Departmental Secretary Li Zong followed on foot, never forsaking the proprieties of office, and still wept over his corpse.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Jin of Xinxing was put to death, his staff scattered — only Departmental Secretary Li Zong walked in attendance, observing every duty of office, and wept over the body.

sentences.zh: 姚元之聞之，曰：「欒布之儔也。」

translations.literal: Yao Yuanzhi heard of it and said, "A man in the company of Luan Bu."
translations.idiomatic: When Yao Yuanzhi heard of it he said, "A man in the mold of Luan Bu."

sentences.zh: 及為相，擢為尚書郎。

translations.literal: When he became chancellor, he promoted him to Secretariat Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Once he took office as chancellor, he raised Li Zong to Secretariat Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 己酉，以刑部尚書趙彥昭為朔方道大總管。

translations.literal: On jiyou, Minister of Justice Zhao Yanzhao was appointed Grand general of the Shuofang circuit.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou day Minister of Justice Zhao Yanzhao was made Grand general of the Shuofang circuit.

sentences.zh: 十一月，乙丑，劉幽求兼侍中。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on yichou, Liu Youqiu was additionally appointed Attendant-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on yichou day, Liu Youqiu was also named Attendant-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，群臣上表請加尊號為開元神武皇帝；

translations.literal: On xinsi, the officials submitted a memorial requesting that his honorific title be augmented to Divine Martial Emperor of Kaiyuan;
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi day the officials memorialized asking that his honorific title be raised to Divine Martial Emperor of Kaiyuan;

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: It was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 戊子，受冊。

translations.literal: On wuzi, he received the investiture.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi day he received the ceremonial investiture.

sentences.zh: 中書侍郎王琚為上所親厚，群臣莫及。

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Secretariat Wang Ju was especially favored by the emperor; no official could match him.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director of the Secretariat Wang Ju was closer to the emperor than any other minister.

sentences.zh: 每進見，侍笑語，逮夜方出。

translations.literal: Whenever he entered audience, he lingered in conversation and laughter and did not leave until night.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he attended audience they talked and laughed together until nightfall.

sentences.zh: 或時休沐，往往遣中使召之。

translations.literal: Even on days of rest, the emperor often sent palace emissaries to summon him.
translations.idiomatic: Even on his days of leave the emperor often sent palace envoys to fetch him.

sentences.zh: 或言於上曰：「王琚權譎縱橫之才，可與之定禍亂，難與之守承平。」

translations.literal: Someone said to the emperor, "Wang Ju possesses a talent for cunning and flexible stratagems — fit to settle turmoil with him, hard to keep peace with him."
translations.idiomatic: Someone told the emperor, "Wang Ju is a man of crafty, shifting talent — useful in chaos, dangerous in peace."

sentences.zh: 上由是浸疏之。

translations.literal: The emperor therefore gradually distanced himself from him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor therefore slowly drew away from him.

sentences.zh: 是月，命琚兼御史大夫，按行北邊諸軍。

translations.literal: That month he ordered Ju to additionally serve as Censor-in-chief and inspect the northern border armies.
translations.idiomatic: That month he ordered Wang Ju to serve concurrently as Censor-in-chief and tour the northern frontier armies.

sentences.zh: 十二月，庚寅，赦天下，改元。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on gengyin, he pardoned the realm and changed the reign era.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on gengyin day, he proclaimed a general amnesty and changed the reign title.

sentences.zh: 尚書左、右僕射為左、右丞相；

translations.literal: Left and Right Vice Directors of the Department of State Affairs were renamed Left and Right Chancellors;
translations.idiomatic: The Left and Right Vice Directors of the Department of State Affairs became the Left and Right Chancellors;

sentences.zh: 中書省為紫微省；

translations.literal: the Secretariat was renamed the Purple Palace Secretariat;
translations.idiomatic: the Secretariat was renamed the Purple Palace Secretariat;

sentences.zh: 門下省為黃門省，侍中為監；

translations.literal: the Chancellery was renamed the Yellow Gate Department, and Attendants-in-chief were renamed Supervisors;
translations.idiomatic: the Chancellery became the Yellow Gate Department, and Attendants-in-chief were retitled Supervisors;

sentences.zh: 雍州為京兆府，洛州為河南府，長史為尹，司馬為少尹。

translations.literal: Yong Prefecture became Jingzhao Prefecture, Luo Prefecture became Henan Prefecture, chief secretaries became prefects (Yin), and vice prefects (Sima) became junior prefects (Shaoyin).
translations.idiomatic: Yongzhou became Jingzhao Prefecture and Luozhou Henan Prefecture; chief secretaries were renamed prefects (Yin), and vice prefects (Sima) junior prefects (Shaoyin).

sentences.zh: 甲午，吐蕃遣其大臣來求和。

translations.literal: On jiawu, Tibet sent its great minister to sue for peace.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu day Tibet dispatched a senior minister to seek peace.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，以姚元之兼紫微令。

translations.literal: On renyin, Yao Yuanzhi was additionally appointed Director of the Purple Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin day Yao Yuanzhi was also named Director of the Purple Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 元之避開元尊號，復名崇。

translations.literal: Yuanzhi avoided the Kaiyuan honorific and resumed his original name Chong.
translations.idiomatic: To avoid the Kaiyuan honorific, Yuanzhi took back his original name, Chong.

sentences.zh: 敕：「都督、刺史、都護將之官，皆引面辭畢，側門取進止。」

translations.literal: An edict stated, "When area commanders, prefects, and protector-generals take up their posts, all shall be led in for a farewell audience; thereafter they shall receive their final orders at the side gate."
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared: "Area commanders, prefects, and protector-generals departing for their posts must all be presented for a farewell audience; when that is done, they shall receive their final instructions at the side gate."

sentences.zh: 姚崇即為相，紫微令張說懼，乃潛詣岐王申款。

translations.literal: Once Yao Chong had become chancellor, Purple Palace Secretariat Director Zhang Shuo was afraid and secretly went to seek favor with the Prince of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: After Yao Chong became chancellor, Purple Palace Secretariat Director Zhang Shuo grew fearful and secretly went to pay court to the Prince of Qi.

sentences.zh: 他日，崇對於便殿，行微蹇。

translations.literal: Another day, Chong was answering in the informal hall and walked with a slight limp.
translations.idiomatic: On another day Chong answered the emperor in the informal hall, walking with a slight hobble.

sentences.zh: 上問：「有足疾乎？」

translations.literal: The emperor asked, "Do you have an ailment of the foot?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, "Is your foot troubling you?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣有腹心之疾，非足疾也。」

translations.literal: He replied, "Your subject has an ailment of the heart and bowels, not of the foot."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Your subject suffers from a trouble of the heart, not of the foot."

sentences.zh: 上問其故。

translations.literal: The emperor asked the reason.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked what he meant.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「岐王陛下愛弟，張說為輔臣，而密乘車入王家，恐為所誤，故憂之。」

translations.literal: He replied, "The Prince of Qi is Your Majesty's beloved younger brother; Zhang Shuo is an assisting minister, yet he secretly rode a carriage into the princely household — I fear he may be led astray, and so I am troubled."
translations.idiomatic: He said, "The Prince of Qi is Your Majesty's beloved brother; Zhang Shuo is a chief minister, yet he secretly rode into the princely house in a carriage. I fear Your Majesty's brother may be led astray — that is my trouble."

sentences.zh: 癸丑，說左遷相州刺史。

translations.literal: On guichou, Shuo was demoted to prefect of Xiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou day Zhang Shuo was demoted to prefect of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 右僕射、同中書門下三品劉幽求亦罷為太子少保。

translations.literal: Right Vice Director Liu Youqiu, Associate of the Three Departments, was also removed and made Crown Prince's Junior Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: Right Vice Director Liu Youqiu, Associate of the Three Departments, was also dismissed and made Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，以黃門侍郎盧懷慎同紫微黃門平章事。

translations.literal: On jiayin, Yellow Gate Vice Director Lu Huaishen was appointed Grand Councilor concurrently of the Purple Palace and Yellow Gate Departments.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin day Yellow Gate Vice Director Lu Huaishen was made Grand Councilor of the Purple Palace and Yellow Gate Departments.
